articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 2
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks drops the WR Blueprint for Week 2.
articles.body:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically every thing that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be a RB column , this WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions . You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every rankings thoroughly by Thursday Night Football, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available .

Note: Total-yardage projections are based on betting markets.

1. Puka Nacua (vs. NYG) - 85.5 proj. receiving yards

Matthew Stafford was brutal in Week 1. He wasn't seeing things well and made life way harder than needed. That's the outlier game, and even then, Nacua was the WR11 in expected half-PPR points (13.0) despite not finishing the game with starters on the field.

This week's matchup is far more normal. First, it's in the United States. Second, it's not a divisional opponent from the same coaching tree. Third, the Giants' starting CBs are in the midst of tryouts for snaps. It's a cupcake matchup for Nacua, who did something in Week 1 that wasn't the case in 2025 when he was the clear-cut WR1 overall in fantasy: play in 1-WR set snaps at the goal line. That can't be understated after Davante Adams goal-line-faded his way to a top-10 fantasy season in 2025 solely off that role.

2. Amon-Ra St. Brown (at BUF) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

The Sun God had the best usage of any WR in Week 1, according to my expected half-PPR points model (20.8). New OC Drew Petzig typically highlights a slot/TE type to run his offense through, and that's absolutely ARSB this year. Meanwhile, the Lions' OL and DBs are beat up. They're missing their starting LG, C and RT on offense, and both safeties and possibly a starting CB on defense. Detroit will have to pass more because of that, and Jared Goff has already been the QB2 in passing yards in 3-street seasons.

The matchup is a very good one, too. The Lions are projected for 25.0 points (eighth) as 4.5-point dogs in Buffalo. The Bills have a solid CB1 in Christian Benford , but he'll be tasked with Jameson Williams as a boundary player, while St. Brown has the best individual matchup. They've struggled against slot types recently, to the point that St. Brown has a case to be the WR1 overall in Week 2.

3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (at ARI) - 81.5 proj. receiving yards

The drop off from Sam Darnold to Drew Lock is real, but Lock is at least a gunslinger who will give his top guys chances down the field. JSN saved his week one with a hitch against the blitz, where he outran everyone despite a mediocre 40-yard dash time. He still had WR4 expected half-PPR points (17.8) with Lock in a clear win.

This week, the Seahawks are slight favorites with a 22.5-point team total (18th) in Arizona . That defense was surprisingly solid in Week 1 against the Chargers, showing nice communication in zone coverage. They don't have a star CB1, however, and Ladd McConkey was gashing them for chunk plays before his hospital-ball rib injury. JSN has also been extremely efficient in this exact matchup historically:

4. Justin Jefferson (at CHI) - 77.5 proj. receiving yards

In 54 games since 2022 without J.J. McCarthy , Jefferson is the WR3 on WR7 usage, averaging 95 YPG and 107 air yards per game. In six games with Carson Wentz , Jefferson is the WR4 on WR7 usage, averaging 95 YPG and 105 air yards per game. In other words, Wentz has been generally as good at getting Jefferson the ball as the rest of the Vikings QBs recently.

The Bears were a mess in Week 1 with SCB Kyler Gordon and S Coby Bryant sidelined. Jalen Coker finished as the WR1 overall, while Tetairoa McMillan had 119 air yards. This was the same thing that happened in 2025, when the Bears allowed the second-most fantasy points to WRs. With DC Dennis Allen, they're going to live and die with their man coverage ability. They had the second-highest man coverage rate of Week 1. Long story short, this is a great spot. The Vikings are projected for 22.0 points (19th) in projected negative game script as slight road dogs.

5. Ja'Marr Chase (at HOU) - 75.5 proj. receiving yards

Chase had the rare dud with Joe Burrow healthy. There were some slight differences in the offense, but nothing too drastic. The Bengals were third in neutral pass rate still. Chase had a fade to the goal line that went incomplete and did stumble at the top of an in-cut on another target, so perhaps he's still working back from his hyperextended knee in camp. He looked fast in a straight line, caught a screen and hit a toe-tapper on the sideline. Things will even out.

The Texans obviously are a horrible draw for Week 2. The Bengals only project for 21.75 points (20th) in Houston , who have two great CBs to match up with both WRs. In 2025, the Texans were fifth-best against fantasy WRs, allowing just 200 total passing yards to all positions. Chase did face the Texans in Week 10 of 2023 and he hung 5-124-1 on six targets on them, for what it's worth.

6. CeeDee Lamb (vs. WAS) - 75.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb had a solid debut against the Giants, who bled out the clock and limited the Cowboys offense to just 34 dropbacks and 52 plays. Lamb had his signature 27% target share and 13.4 expected half-PPR points (WR10), which lines up with his splits next to George Pickens from 2025. Lamb averaged 89 receiving yards per game on a 26% target share, if we remove his two injured games. He was the WR8 on WR6 usage, with the only real difference being he scored 0.25 touchdowns per game rather than his baseline of 0.37.

The Commanders are running a new chaotic defense, but their secondary remains in pretty tough shape. Mike Sainristil struggled in the opener, and Lamb has averaged 75 yards on 6.9 receptions in seven games against the Commanders since 2022. He had a 5-110-1 game against them just last year. It's a great spot for Lamb. Dallas has a 27.5-point team total (fifth) at home.

7. George Pickens (vs. WAS) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Pickens had a poor Week 1 outing, just as he did in 2025 before lighting up the league the rest of the way. Pickens dropped an in-cut and downfield sideline go ball, and that was the difference. At the same time, Pickens drew a 41-yard DPI on third down and came away with three underneath catches on strong route running. There's no reason to change our perspective out of Week 1. He had 104 air yards and a 20% target share and 90% route rate. In 14 games with Lamb, Pickens is the WR14 on WR15 usage on a 22% target share, while running less hot than usual on TDs. He's a low-end WR1.

The matchup with the Commanders is a great one. The Cowboys are fifth in projected points (27.5) while at home, and the Commanders allowed splash plays to Dontayvion Wicks (twice), Devonta Smith and Dallas Goedert last week.

8. DJ Moore (vs. DET) - 63.5 proj. receiving yards

Moore had a very promising debut, beyond just scoring 18.5-half PPR points. His 43-yard TD was out of structure because Josh Allen is a wizard, but he also had a slot target and multiple downfield shots. He drew a 47-yard DPI in the end zone off an under-center play action and another defensive holding down the field, then was given two other prayer shots down the field. That all led to 158 air yards (WR3).

The Bills project for the most points of Week 2, and the Lions secondary is extremely beat up. Their top two safeties are out, and CB2 DJ Reed (foot) is questionable. Even last year, the Lions allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs. Then they were lit up by WRs Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele down the field in Week 2, and that's exactly where Moore is going to operate in this offense. It's as tasty of a matchup as he'll get all year.

9. Chris Olave (at BAL) - 74.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave has 10 games with Tyler Shough now. He's the WR4 (15.9 half-PPR points) on WR7 usage in them, averaging 91 yards on 139 air yards and 9.8 targets per game. This is an elite role at least until Jordyn Tyson comes back in the mix. The Saints were first in neutral pace in 2025 and followed that up in Week 1, when the offense was lighting up the Lions in the second half and overtime. They ran 86 plays!!!

This matchup is the polar opposite. The Ravens defense was flying around the field in Week 1 with star players littered in the secondary. He'll likely see a ton of CB1 Nate Wiggins , who has the speed to match with Olave down the field. They also have new HC Jesse Minter to use superstar S Kyle Hamilton as they see fit. They allowed -0.44 EPA per dropback last week. Because of this potentially great defense, the Saints only project for 19.0 points (27th). Olave also popped up with a hamstring injury on Thursday; something to monitor.

10. Garrett Wilson (vs. GB) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards

The Jets took care of business against the Titans in Week 1. Wilson and Geno Smith looked great on film, and the pass game flowed through the former still. He had another 30% target share, which will lead to even bigger games when they're playing in negative game script.

The Packers are a great matchup for Wilson. Green Bay 's offense can't run the ball, and their pass-game looks extremely explosive. They could put up points in a hurry or punt the ball quickly, leading to more plays for the Jets, who are 3.5-point dogs at home. Green Bay's defense is also a weakness. They're sixth-worst in EPA per dropback and second-worst in sack rate since Week 15 of last year when Micah Parsons went down.

11. Mike Evans (vs. MIA) - 48.5 proj. receiving yards

Unc still got it. Evans looked great in a slightly altered role in his Week 1 debut against a loaded secondary. The Niners got him on a few quick out routes, then gave him a signature end-zone fade for a TD. It was a clean 21% target share, and those targets will be very efficient in this offense. Beyond that, De'Zhaun Stribling's snaps will be replaced by low-volume clear-out WR Demarcus Robinson and George Kittle didn't look like himself on tape. It's a great spot all around.

This week's matchup does not get any easier. The 49ers are second in projected points (29.0) against the Dolphins, who have the youngest defense in the NFL by far. They're trotting out a rookie CB, and Chris Johnson was lit up for double-digit targets in the opener. Expect Evans to see bust CB1 JuJu Brents plenty. BBQ chicken.

12. Malik Nabers (at LAR) - 65.5 proj. receiving yards

Nabers ran a route on 71% of dropbacks in his return from multiple knee surgeries, leading to an elite 31% target share, 103 air yards and WR14 expected half-PPR points. On tape, Nabers looked explosive in a straight line and he still was able to make a few impressive cuts after the catch. He did slip three times at the top of his route while breaking left and back towards the ball. We can live with that as he ramps back up over the next month or so. In the meantime, Nabers' role and quality of play are absolutely worth starting, even if he's not quite in the top 12 yet. He's on the path of getting there by the time fantasy matchups have real dollars at stake.

The Rams have stars in the secondary, but they at least won't have Myles Garrett and potentially won't have Aaron Donald yet. If the Rams offense returns to form back in the United States, then Nabers should have plenty of targets in a more favorable game script. The Giants are 7-point dogs with a 20.75-point team total.

13. DeVonta Smith (at TEN) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

The Eagles had some issues on the ground, but they hit chunk plays in the air and did enough schematically against a unique Commanders defense to give us confidence with Smith and Jalen Hurts . Smith is going to be boom-bust, as they seemed to tailor their manufactured touches to first-round slot Makai Lemon instead. Smith still had a 27% target share with a 13.2 average depth of target, a nice sweet spot in my opinion. His -12.2% completion percentage over expectation will normalize, and he should be a good WR2 in fantasy on average.

The matchup is a nice one here. The Titans couldn't stop the Jets in Week 1, and the Eagles are projected for 23.25 points (14th) despite being on the road. The Titans' top outside CBs are pretty volatile, Alontae Taylor (who should be a slot CB imo) and Cor'Dale Flott and Smith is one of the best cross-over route runners in the league.

14. Christian Watson (at NYJ) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

Green Bay's OL can't run block, and their RBs can't hit the hole either. They opted to be eighth in neutral pass rate (60%) and second in neutral pace instead. They've been bottom in each category since Josh Jacobs arrived years ago. It's a big deal. Beyond that, the Packers didn't rotate their WRs much. Watson and Matthew Golden are near full-time players, soaking up 20% and 30% of the targets, respectively. Watson hit the gas on an in-cut for an 81-yarder, then had a manufactured target at the goal line for a second score. It all led to WR12 expected half-PPR points in Week 1. He's a model breaker on top of that.

The matchup is a very clean one. The Jets offense looked competent, and their defense is missing star players in the secondary. Watson will face off with boom-bust CBs AZ Thomas and Brandon Stephens on the perimeter. It doesn't look like the Jets will have S Minkah Fitzpatrick or EDGE Joseph Ossai either. The Packers are projected for 24.0 points (13th).

15. Emeka Egbuka (vs. CLE) - 54.5 proj. receiving yards

Egbuka was fine in Week 1 (WR33 on WR36 usage), but the film was quite promising. He looked healthy on his toe and was very clearly more athletic than Chris Godwin Jr., who was used as a physical power slot underneath. Egbuka ran more digs and had all of the fun motion plays. They leaked him often, had him run through the B gap a couple of times and was targeted deep downfield on a motion-wheel. It was very Rams-coded (bullish). When Baker Mayfield feels less skittish, then Egbuka should have big games ahead.

The Browns had issues with the Jaguars in Week 1, only pressuring that mediocre OL on four dropbacks. They allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs. Parker Washington , who plays the same role in the same coaching tree, had multiple explosives, including a corner route TD from the slot. Ebguka will see some CB1 Denzel Ward , but it will not be the entire time at all. Tampa Bay has a 25.0-point team total (ninth). It's a good matchup.

16. Parker Washington (at DEN) - 55.5 proj. receiving yards

Since Week 7 of last year, Washington is the WR14 on WR12 usage on a per-game basis. That's a 23% target share on a quality offense.

Washington ran a route on 72% of dropbacks, which was a bit lower than expected. He played almost all of the 3-WR sets, splitting time between Z and the slot. He rotated in the non 3-WR set snaps, however, losing some playing time to rookie WR Josh Cameron and others. That said, he's clearly the top target whenever he's out there. Washington led with an elite 29% target share and 102 air yards. He roasted a SCB for a man-coverage corner route TD and had multiple crossing-route wins. He added a one-handed grab on a quick out for good measure. It all led to a WR10 start on WR29 usage in a blowout win.

The matchup is far more difficult this week. The Jaguars are on the road, projecting for 21.5 points (20th) in Denver . Since 2025, the Broncos have been the best defense against fantasy WRs when adjusting for schedule. He won't see much of CB1 Patrick Surtain at least, but CB2 Riley Moss and SCB Ja'Quan McMillan are above average in their roles … but as I pull up the Broncos' box scores, I find that the receiver who had the best fantasy game against them was Mr. Washington himself (6-145-1 on 10 targets in Week 16).

17. Tetairoa McMillan (at ATL) - 57.5 proj. receiving yards

McMillan was just fine in Week 1. He ran a couple of great routes and remains an awesome big-body target in clutch situations. His WR22 expected points were nothing to sneeze at, but McMillan did look a step slower on some of the crossing and go routes versus last year, if we want to over analyze it.

He should be more physical at the catch point and in after-catch situations, but the real Week 1 takeaway is the gap between McMillan and Coker was too large in drafts. That mostly means Coker is flying up rest-of-season rankings than McMillan is tanking. However, McMillan is the WR28 on WR35 usage in eight games since Jalen Coker was a full-time player in Week 12 of last year. Their target shares are Coker, 23% and McMillan, 22%.

McMillan and Coker both play inside and out, but McMillan will generally get the top corner when all else is equal. The Falcons have a good one in A.J. Terrell here. That didn't stop McMillan from a monster 8-130-2 outing the last time they faced off. That was the most fantasy points Atlanta allowed all year.

18. Jaylen Waddle (vs. JAX) - 52.5 proj. receiving yards

Waddle flopped in Week 1. He had an 11% target share and 13 air yards. Come on!!! The potential long-term thorn here could be second-year WR Pat Bryant 's 22% target share. If there are three real weapons at WR, it's always harder to make the math work.

It's shocking to see Waddle's floor be so low, but the good news, if any, is the tape showed a lot more schemed-up opportunities for him than what the box score showed. Bo Nix turned down a swing pass, corner route and pick-wheel in the first half alone. They gave him a route out of the backfield, a third-and-4 choice route, a screen, plenty of switch releases, work out of the slot (59% of snaps), a third-and-7 slant (dropped) and more. The game plan seemed to prioritize Waddle a lot more than Nix allowed. It was more of a QB and C/RB/TE blocking thing than a scheme thing to me. The Broncos were first in neutral pass rate (72%), so the uptick in routes for Waddle should be a real thing.

We'll learn more about his availability (ribs) later in the week.

20. Terry McLaurin (at DAL) - 53.5 proj. receiving yards

McLaurin was predictably shut down by Eagles DC Vic Fangio and elite CB1 Quinyon Mitchell . Even with that dud, McLaurin is the WR14 on WR29 usage in games with Jayden Daniels . The top end of that outcome is very unlikely to repeat after running pure on touchdowns in 2024, but let's not panic here.

Especially not this week. The Cowboys struggled with communication in Week 1 against the Giants, to the point Jaxson Dart had a +0.71 EPA per dropback and Week 1 high 71% success rate. Since 2024, the Cowboys are allowing the most fantasy points to WRs when adjusting for schedule. McLaurin has had two big games within that:

21. Tee Higgins (at HOU) - 55.5 proj. receiving yards

Higgins had a wild 19.5 average depth of target on his six targets in Week 1, leading to an elite 117 air yards. Some of it was performative under-center heaves from Joe Burrow, but those looks are very valuable and I'd guess the Bengals keep up their under-center play-action looks as a third pitch in the offense. Burrow had a 14.3 aDOT under center versus a 6.3 aDOT in the gun on a half second quicker time to throw. Higgins is the WR16 on WR24 usage since 2025 with Burrow in the lineup, and he was even better than that in 2024. Nothing has really changed.

Unfortunately, this is a difficult spot. Burrow seems a bit banged up, and the Texans were the fifth-best defense against fantasy WRs last year with a secondary that all could make the Pro Bowl. Cincy's team total is lower than usual at 22.0 points (19th).

22. Davante Adams (vs. NYG) - 44.5 proj. receiving yards

23. Matthew Golden (at NYJ) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

24. Jameson Williams (at BUF) - 57.5 proj. receiving yards

Williams will have a very boom-bust role with Sam LaPorta healthy. In nine games since 2025 with LaPorta available, Williams is the WR43 on WR54 usage in half PPR, even though he's averaged 10.0 YPT in that sample. Williams' average depth of target climbs to 14.8 yards downfield as the primary clear out player. That was his role in Week 1, when he came up close to empty on 127 air yards (!!!) and 13.9 expected half-PPR points (WR7). There will be WR50 weeks. There will be WR5 weeks. They'll just be hard to predict before the week.

Williams' individual matchup is solid. The Lions are projected for 25.0 points and are set up in more pass-heavy script as road dogs. The Lions are missing 3-of-5 OL starters and multiple DBs, so don't be surprised if Goff drops back a ton. Jamo will face shadow CB1 Christian Benford on the perimeter and he had an up-and-down game against Nico Collins in Week 1, traveling with him on each side of the field.

25. DK Metcalf (at NE) - 50.5 proj. receiving yards

Metcalf had excellent usage in Week 1. He was the WR6 in expected half-PPR points (15.0) on 204 air yards and a 27% target share. It helped that the Steelers were fifth in neutral pass rate (66%) in new HC Mike McCarthy's debut, far higher than last year's 54%. Was it effective? Nope. He had a drop over the middle, an OPI on an out route and a few near completions way down the field. We'll see if the Steelers felt like last week's game plan holds as September rolls on, but this was a far more downfield role (20.4 average depth of target) for their WR1.

The matchup is a difficult one. The Patriots have elite CB1 Christian Gonzalez, who has the size and speed to match up with Metcalf. New England allowed just 201 YPG through the air in 2025. He had 35 yards in this matchup in Week 3 of last year, too. Pittsburgh has things to work on, and the betting markets agree, as they have the 29th team total of Week 2 (18.0).

26. Drake London (vs. CAR) - 56.5 proj. receiving yards

Don't read too much into the Falcons' Week 1 brutal start, unless Cooper Rush continues to start. We'll learn more later in the week. This assumes it's Rush again.

The bigger thing to note from Week 1 was the minor changes in the offense. London's slot rate fell from 34% last year to 16% in Week 1. He's an excellent big slot, so losing some of that work will hurt the margins.

27. Rome Odunze (vs. MIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

28. Jalen Coker (at ATL) - 50.5 proj. receiving yards

Jalen Coker started and played 82% snaps in Week 12 of last year. In eight games since then, he's the WR11 on WR27 usage in half PPR. He's running really hot, but the usage is real and he is undeniably a good player. Without much depth in Carolina, he might be a fantasy WR3.

29. Luther Burden (vs. MIN) - 51.5 proj. receiving yards

30. Rashee Rice (vs. IND) - 53.5 proj. receiving yards

Rice scored a 13-yard touchdown, bouncing off two defenders on a 1-on-1 "screen." He only had six receiving yards on 26 non-screen routes, however. The Chiefs offense also flipped, as expected. They had a 58% neutral pass rate over the past three seasons, then in Week 1 with Kenneth Walker dominating, the Chiefs had a 48% neutral pass rate. That'll hurt Rice' PPR-scam ability. The good news is the pass game remained quite dink-and-dunk, but it's still unclear just how healthy Rice is after a second knee surgery this offseason. He looked just fine to me. His 3.3 expected half-PPR points (WR88) and 8% target share has to be nerve-racking for Round 3 drafters, though (not me).

The Colts were gashed in Week 1, but they did play the most man coverage (56%) and that's exactly what gives Rice issues. 2025 third-round SCB Justin Walley made his debut after injury last week, and it didn't go well. The individual matchup is decent, but Rice will have to buck his trend of being a total non-factor against man. The Chiefs are projected for 26.5 points (sixth) at home.

31. Deebo Samuel (vs. MIA) - 35.5 proj. receiving yards

33. Stefon Diggs (at DAL) - 46.5 proj. receiving yards

34. Alec Pierce (at KC) - 45.5 proj. receiving yards

35. Chris Godwin Jr. (vs. CLE) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Godwin is out of his prime on tape. He did absolutely yeet a couple of Bengals tacklers after the catch with grown-man strength, but his speed is officially lackluster, as it was last season. He was targeted four times, three of which were behind the line of scrimmage. Emeka Egbuka was given more at-snap motion responsibilities as the primary intermediate target on the team. Godwin had the negative game script last week, yet mustered just a 15% target share. He's a WR4 bench stash while everyone is healthy. He could be a mid-volume, red-zone threat to wind down his career.

36. Jayden Reed (at NYJ) - 37.5 proj. receiving yards

articles.title: Saints news: Tyler Shough gets 'poor man's Josh Allen' comparison from DC
articles.summary: Tyler Shough is only entering the second game of his second NFL season, but he’s already drawing comparisons to one of the league’s biggest superstars. Balti...
articles.body:
Tyler Shough is only entering the second game of his second NFL season, but he's already drawing comparisons to one of the league's biggest superstars.

Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said Thursday that Shough reminds him of a "poor man's Josh Allen ," pointing specifically to the New Orleans Saints quarterback's arm strength and mobility.

Weaver knows firsthand what Shough can do. While serving as Miami 's defensive coordinator last season, Weaver watched Shough throw for 239 yards and two touchdowns against the Dolphins.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Now Shough looks considerably more comfortable. The 26-year-old opened his second season by completing 35 of 56 passes for a career-high 410 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions in New Orleans ' 31-30 overtime loss to Detroit . New Orleans fell behind 21-0 before Shough and the offense finally came alive . The Saints scored on five of their final six possessions and eventually forced overtime before falling short on a two-point conversion attempt.

That's the version of Shough that should have Saints fans excited. Nobody is putting him in Allen's class after one 400-yard performance. Allen himself needed time before developing into one of the NFL's premier quarterbacks.

Shough has plenty of time to establish his own identity in Kellen Moore's offense. New Orleans isn't loaded with the type of roster that will make life easy for its young quarterback, either. That makes Shough's development one of the most important storylines surrounding the Saints this season.

Baltimore will provide another difficult test Sunday. If Shough can follow his Week 1 performance with another impressive showing against Weaver's defense, that "poor man's Josh Allen " comparison might start sounding a little more complimentary.

articles.title: How Novak Djokovic performed in his first-ever China Open as he announces 2026 return
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic is set to compete at the China Open for the first time in 11 years. With six China Open titles to his name,...
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic is set to compete at the China Open for the first time in 11 years.

With six China Open titles to his name, Djokovic is the most successful male player in tournament history.

The Serbian superstar, who recently exited the ATP top 10 after losing in the US Open first round, confirmed his participation in the 2026 event in a social media video posted on Wednesday.

Djokovic made his first-ever appearance at the Beijing-based event in 2009.

How did the tennis icon perform on his debut?

Novak Djokovic won the China Open on debut

Djokovic entered the 2009 China Open as the second seed, behind only Rafael Nadal.

The Serb handled his first two rounds with ease, defeating Victor Hanescu and compatriot Viktor Troicki in straight sets.

He then survived a scare against Fernando Verdasco in the quarter-finals, triumphing 6-3, 1-6, 6-1 in the Chinese capital.

Djokovic defeated Robin Soderling 6-3, 6-3 in the semi-finals, setting up a clash with 2014 US Open champion Marin Cilic.

Cilic, the eighth-seeded wildcard entry, stunned top seed Rafael Nadal in the semi-finals.

Djokovic proved too strong for the Croatian, claiming his first China Open title with a 6-2, 7-6 victory.

Djokovic went on to claim six China Open titles in seven years, including four in a row between 2012 and 2015.

2009: defeated Marin Cilic in the final, 6–2, 7–6

2010: defeated David Ferrer in the final, 6–2, 6–4

2012: defeated Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in the final, 7–6, 6–2

2013: defeated Rafael Nadal in the final, 6–3, 6–4

2014: defeated Tomas Berdych in the final, 6–0, 6–2

2015: defeated Rafael Nadal in the final, 6–2, 6–2

What did Novak Djokovic say ahead of winning the 2015 China Open?

In 2015, Only Rafael Nadal stood in the way of Novak Djokovic winning a sixth China Open title.

Prior to the final in Beijing, Djokovic described his record in China as one of his greatest accomplishments as a tennis player.

"This is right at the top, one of the best achievements I've had in my career," Djokovic stated prior to playing Nadal.

"Every time I keep coming back, I have these positive, great memories from the success, the great performances I had on the centre court, support, just overall feel is very positive.

Djokovic defeated Nadal in emphatic fashion, triumphing 6-2, 6-2.

Djokovic has only lost one match at the China Open : Novak and Djordje Djokovic were beaten by Vasek Pospisil and Jack Sock in the 2015 men's doubles event.

articles.title: Jonathan Bale grabs lead at 101st Crump Memorial
articles.summary: Jonathan Bale shot a 1-over-par 71 to take the lead at the 101st George Arthur Crump Memorial at Pine Valley.
articles.body:
Jonathan Bale made three birdies on the back nine and shot a 1-over par 71 in the first round of stroke-play qualifying of the 101st annual George Arthur Crump Memorial Tournament at Pine Valley.

Bale, a resident of Jupiter, Florida, leads a logjam of players two strokes off the pace that includes Chadd Slutzky of Deer Park, Illinois, Drew Kittleson of Scottsdale, Arizona, Gregor Orlando of Haverford, Pennsylvania, Andrew Bailey of Shaker Heights, Ohio, U.S. Walker Cupper Stewart Hagestad of Hermosa Beach, California, Chris Wheeler of Lewisville, Texas, and Chad Wilfong of Charlotte, North Carolina. Defending champion Bobby Wyatt has his work cut out to make match play after opening with 77.

A trio of past senior champions lead the Senior Division at 74. Michael McCoy of Norwalk, Iowa, Jamie Slonis of Sewell, New Jersey, and Tommy Brennan of Covington, Louisiana finished two strokes better than defending senior champion Bob Royak of Alpharetta, Georgia.

The Open division has 78 players competing for 48 spots in match play while 21 senior players are contending for 16 spots.

The Crump Cup is arguably the premier mid-amateur tournament in the United States. Pine Valley is ranked second in the latest Golfweek's Best Classic Courses list.

Pine Valley Golf Club will not be open to the public for Sunday's final match of the 2026 Crump Memorial Tournament as had been the case pre-COVID.

articles.title: Nolan Wells case update: Court hears disturbing allegations before judge orders suspect jailed without bond
articles.summary: International Sports News: A federal judge in Mississippi has ordered Edward James Porter to remain in custody without bond after prosecutors challenged his release in a case in.
articles.body: A federal judge in Mississippi has ordered Edward James Porter to remain in custody without bond after prosecutors challenged his release in a case involving alleged threats against a witness connected to the investigation into Nolan Xavier Wells’ death. The ruling followed an emergency hearing where an FBI agent described repeated calls and threats allegedly directed at Bart Edmiston Jr. and his family.Edward James Porter remains jailed after alleged threatsU.S. District Judge Taylor McNeel ruled that Porter should remain behind bars while his federal case proceeds. Prosecutors had sought an emergency hearing after another federal judge in Illinois had granted him bond.During the Sept. 9 hearing, FBI Task Force Agent Christopher Kloc testified about a series of calls allegedly made by Porter on July 31. According to the testimony reported by the Sun Herald, Porter allegedly used Pinger to disguise his actual phone number and make the calls appear to originate from Moss Point, Mississippi.Kloc said Porter made 12 calls to Bart Edmiston Jr. and his father over roughly three hours. Prosecutors allege that the calls included threats against the family.Edmiston Jr., 21, is a friend of Nolan Wells and currently plays football at the University of Wyoming. His name appeared in a Mississippi Department of Marine Resources incident report after he helped tow a boat connected to the events surrounding Wells' disappearance.The threats came weeks after Wells, 18, disappeared following a Fourth of July trip to Horn Island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. His body was found on July 6. Authorities have not charged anyone in connection with Wells' death.What the court heard about the alleged threatsThe testimony presented a troubling picture of the alleged communications. Kloc told the court that Porter had Edmiston Jr.'s childhood address in Ocean Springs and allegedly sent it to him by text.According to testimony, Porter also contacted Edmiston Sr. while he was undergoing a medical procedure. The FBI agent said Porter allegedly threatened the older man, his household and responding police officers.Porter later allegedly told Edmiston Jr. that he was outside the family's Ocean Springs home and threatened to kill the family, according to the testimony.The judge also considered Porter's previous criminal record. The court was told that he had faced numerous violent criminal charges over the years, including allegations involving assault, assault with a deadly weapon and domestic violence. The pretrial report also showed that he had forfeited bond 13 times and had a pending fugitive-from-justice charge.Porter was unemployed and living at a homeless shelter when he was arrested in Illinois. His sister offered to let him stay with her, but she told the court she would be away at work during the day and could not supervise him.McNeel ultimately determined that Porter presented a flight risk and a danger to the victims and community. The judge concluded that detention was necessary because available release conditions could not reasonably guarantee safety or ensure Porter's appearance in future proceedings.Porter is not the only person facing federal allegations connected to threats surrounding the Wells investigation. Brandon Ephriam Washington of Jacksonville, Florida, is separately accused of sending threatening messages to Edmiston Jr. and remains free on bond pending his case in Wyoming.The Wells investigation itself remains separate from these federal threat cases. No one has been charged with causing Wells' death, and authorities continue to investigate what happened after he disappeared during the July Fourth trip.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf bought a 3.5-acre California estate for $23 million; after four years on the market, it sold for $20 million following an initial $24.5 million listing
articles.summary: International Sports News: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s former California home took almost four years to sell after the tennis stars put it on the market. The couple had paid .
articles.body: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s former California home took almost four years to sell after the tennis stars put it on the market. The couple had paid about $23 million for the 3.5-acre Roundhill Estate in Tiburon, California, making it a record residential sale in Marin County at the time. They first listed the property for $24.5 million in 2003, but the asking price was cut several times before the estate finally sold for $20 million in 2006. The sale left Agassi and Graf with a $3 million difference before other ownership costs were counted.Why did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf pay $23 million for the Tiburon estateAndre Agassi had already developed a strong connection with the San Francisco Bay Area before buying the property. He regularly played tournaments in Northern California and liked the idea of having a private place there.In December 2000, Agassi paid about $23 million for the Tiburon estate, which was then one of the biggest residential deals in Marin County. The property had previously belonged to John E. McCaw Jr., the former Cellular One owner.The location was a major part of its appeal. The estate sat on about 3.5 acres above the San Francisco Bay and had views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco skyline. It also came with a six-bedroom, eight-bathroom home and large outdoor areas.SFGate reported in February 2001 that Agassi described the property as a place he had come to love. “Make no bones about it – I travel 30 weeks-plus a year, and this is a place I’ve come to love, and it’s been a vacation place,” he said.At the time, the home was not only a luxury property but also a practical getaway for a tennis player who spent much of the year travelling. Agassi said it would be a part-time vacation home rather than his main base.The estate also had two swimming pools, a tennis court, a squash court and a four-bedroom staff house. Contemporary reports put the main residence at about 10,500 square feet, while other descriptions gave larger figures when additional buildings were included.What made Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s California home unusualThe tennis connection was hard to miss. The estate had its own tennis court, giving Agassi and Graf a private place to play away from the public.That mattered because both were still closely linked to professional tennis when the property was purchased. Graf had retired in 1999 after winning 22 Grand Slam singles titles. Agassi continued playing for several more years and eventually retired after the 2006 US Open.The property was also built for a large family and frequent guests. Along with the main house, there were separate staff quarters and additional guest space. Reports also mentioned two pools, several spa areas, a hydrotherapy waterfall and a large private lot.The home had already undergone a major renovation before Agassi bought it. It was built in 1976, and John E. McCaw Jr. had carried out the last major renovation in the 1990s.Still, the house did not remain an easy sell later. When the property went back on the market, its older design became one of the issues affecting interest. Listing agent Bill Bullock told the San Francisco Chronicle that the house had a “dated feel,” which made the sale harder.The size and price were another challenge. A buyer needed to be willing to spend tens of millions of dollars on one property, and the pool of people looking at homes at that level was small.Why did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf list the $23 million estate for $24.5 millionBy the time the Tiburon home was listed in 2003, the couple’s lifestyle had changed. Graf had been retired from tennis for several years, while Agassi was still competing but was spending much of his time travelling for tournaments and handling his business interests.The couple also lived primarily in Las Vegas, where Agassi had deep family and business ties. That made the California property less useful as an everyday home.Agassi explained the situation during a 2003 interview. “I’m playing the game a lot longer than I thought. We’re still traveling the world,” he said. “A lot of my business is in Las Vegas and it just doesn’t make sense for us to have a place that doesn’t get used.”They initially asked $24.5 million for the property. That was $1.5 million above what Agassi had paid when he bought it.The estate did not find a buyer quickly. It moved on and off the market, and the asking price was reduced more than once. By 2006, the price had fallen to $21 million.The decision to sell was also tied to the cost of keeping such a large property. Bill Bullock said the couple’s advisers wanted Agassi to dispose of the home because it was being used infrequently.How did Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s estate finally sell for $20 millionAfter nearly four years on the market, the Tiburon estate finally found a buyer in 2006. The buyer was Stuart Peterson, a Marin County resident and head of the investment firm Artis Capital Management.The final price was $20 million, which was $3 million below the couple’s original purchase price. The deal was reported as one of the largest residential sales in Marin County at the time.The San Francisco Chronicle reported that the property had been difficult to sell partly because there were relatively few buyers for homes priced above $20 million. The estate had already gone through several price reductions before Peterson agreed to the $20 million deal.The sale meant Agassi and Graf did not make money from the California property itself. Based only on the purchase and sale prices, they were down $3 million. Their actual financial result would have been different after taxes, maintenance, insurance and real estate commissions were taken into account.For the couple, however, the sale also ended a chapter that no longer fitted their daily life. Graf had long since left professional tennis, and Agassi was nearing the end of his playing career when the property finally changed hands.Their Tiburon home had started as a private escape with views of the Bay Area and a tennis court of its own. By the time it sold, it had become a property the couple rarely used and one that had spent years searching for the right buyer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The peaks are higher, the floor is rising: How India’s Asian Games medal story has changed over two decades
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: “Abki baar, sau paar” was the rallying cry when India arrived at the Hangzhou Asian Games in September 2023.By the time the Games ended, it had become.
articles.body: “Abki baar, sau paar” was the rallying cry when India arrived at the Hangzhou Asian Games in September 2023.By the time the Games ended, it had become more than a slogan. India had crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time in its Asian Games history, eventually finishing with 106 medals — 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze. The 100th medal came through the women's kabaddi team, which defeated Chinese Taipei in the gold-medal match.It was India's biggest-ever medal haul at the Asian Games.But as India prepares for Aichi-Nagoya 2026, the more important story is not that India finally reached 100. It is that 100 no longer looks like an isolated miracle when viewed against Indian sport's larger trajectory.Hangzhou came after four consecutive editions in which India had already crossed 50 medals. India is becoming increasingly consistent.At the Asian Games, 50-plus medals have become the norm. At the Olympics, India has produced multiple medals at five consecutive editions for the first time.India remains an under-achiever. But the direction of travel is increasingly difficult to ignore.From occasional highs to a new Asian Games floorThe strongest evidence of India's sporting evolution is perhaps the simplest: 53 > 65 > 57 > 70 > 106.Those are India's medal tallies at the last five completed Asian Games — Doha 2006, Guangzhou 2010, Incheon 2014, Jakarta 2018 and Hangzhou 2022.Before this run, India had crossed the 50-medal mark only twice in the previous 14 editions. Both came at home.At the inaugural Asian Games in New Delhi in 1951, India won 51 medals, including 15 gold. When New Delhi hosted the Games again in 1982, India collected 57 medals, including 13 gold.It took another 24 years for India to cross 50 again. Doha 2006 changed that.India won 53 medals in Qatar, finally breaking the half-century barrier away from home. It was followed by 65 in Guangzhou, 57 in Incheon and 70 in Jakarta and Palembang. Then came Hangzhou.The five consecutive 50-plus medal campaigns represent something India had never previously achieved at the continental event. That is arguably more significant than the 106 itself.A record medal tally can be an extraordinary peak. Five consecutive campaigns above a particular benchmark point towards a structural change.India has therefore entered Aichi-Nagoya with a different kind of expectation. Another 106 may be difficult, particularly with a 499-athlete contingent compared with the 661 who travelled to Hangzhou.But the benchmark has moved. The question is no longer simply whether India can cross 50. It is whether a 50-medal campaign would now be considered underwhelming.Hangzhou did not just breach 100 — it moved India's ceilingThe jump from Jakarta to Hangzhou was extraordinary.India went from 70 medals in 2018 to 106 in Hangzhou, an increase of 36 medals. But the gold-medal jump arguably tells an even more significant story.India won 16 gold medals in Jakarta. In Hangzhou, it won 28. That is a 75 per cent increase in gold medals in one edition.And India's Hangzhou medal haul (106) was twice its Doha tally (53) over a 17-year period.The 100-medal barrier, therefore, should not be viewed in isolation. India's Asian Games ceiling has moved.It would be unrealistic to treat 106 as an automatic target every time India enters an Asian Games. But if India can produce another 70-plus campaign in Aichi-Nagoya, it would create another significant benchmark — three consecutive editions above 70.That could eventually make 70-plus the next version of what 50-plus has become today. One ceiling becomes the next floor.The medal base is becoming broaderThere is another part of the Asian Games story that is easy to miss when the conversation is dominated by the overall tally.India is not merely winning more medals. Its medal-producing ecosystem is gradually becoming broader.Historically, athletics has been India's biggest Asian Games sport by a considerable distance, with 283 medals. Shooting follows with 80, wrestling with 65, boxing with 61 and lawn tennis with 34.Athletics remains the giant. But recent editions have shown that India's medal ambitions are increasingly supported by multiple disciplines.Hangzhou was an excellent example. Athletics produced 29 medals, shooting contributed 22 and archery added nine. More importantly, shooting produced seven gold medals, one more than athletics' six. That shows the modern Indian medal base is not entirely dependent on its biggest traditional discipline.Wrestling, boxing, squash, archery and tennis have repeatedly provided medal opportunities, while athletics and shooting continue to contribute.The Commonwealth Games in Glasgow in 2026 provided another encouraging indicator for boxing, with Indian boxers winning 10 medals, including seven gold — their best-ever gold-medal haul at the event.India's sporting rise is becoming less dependent on one discipline or one generation. That is what a broader sporting ecosystem looks like.The Olympics tell a quieter story of progressIf the Asian Games provide the dramatic version of India's sporting evolution, the Olympics provide the subtler one.India has won only 41 medals across its entire Olympic history — 10 gold, 10 silver and 21 bronze.For a country of India's size and sporting ambitions, that remains underwhelming. But look at when those medals have arrived.From Beijing 2008 through Paris 2024, India won 24 of its 41 Olympic medals — 58.5 per cent of its entire Olympic medal haul in just five editions.Beijing 2008 produced three medals. London 2012 delivered six. Rio 2016 dropped to two. Tokyo 2020 produced a record seven. Paris 2024 ended with six.The numbers are not spectacular by the standards of sporting superpowers. But historically, they are significant.Before this five-edition run, India had achieved multiple-medal campaigns at only two Olympics — Paris 1900, when Norman Pritchard won two silver medals, and Helsinki 1952, when India won one gold and one bronze.Then came five consecutive Olympic editions with multiple Indian medals. That is the quieter revolution. And the country is no longer disappearing between Games. The consistency itself represents progress.Paris showed how close India remains to a bigger breakthroughThe six-medal haul at Paris 2024 was disappointing because expectations had changed.After India's record-breaking Asian Games campaign a year earlier, there was genuine hope that the country could finally push into double figures at the Olympics.It did not happen. But Paris also showed why the ambition for 10 medals was not completely misplaced.India had several agonising near-misses. The archery mixed team finished fourth after losing its bronze-medal match. Lakshya Sen lost the badminton bronze-medal match. Shooter Arjun Babuta finished fourth in the men's 10m air rifle. Manu Bhaker, already a double medallist, missed out on a third medal after finishing fourth in the women's 25m pistol. India's skeet team lost its bronze-medal shoot-out, while weightlifter Mirabai Chanu finished fourth.Then came Vinesh Phogat's disqualification before her gold-medal bout after she was found 100 grams over the weight limit.Seven “what if” moments.That does not mean India should retrospectively count those as medals. But it demonstrates how narrow the margins can be at the Olympics.Four of those near-misses becoming medals would have taken India to 10.The more important takeaway is that India is beginning to produce enough finalists and medal contenders across different sports for the conversation to shift from “Can India win?” to “How many can India convert?”That is a different challenge. And in many ways, it is a sign of progress.The real evolution: India's floor is risingThe Asian Games and Olympics operate on completely different scales, but together they reveal a striking change in India's sporting story.The underlying pattern is comparable. India's old sporting story was one of sporadic success. Its emerging story is one of sustained presence.At the Asian Games, India has established a 50-medal floor. Hangzhou then pushed the ceiling beyond 100.At the Olympics, India has established something much more modest but historically important: five consecutive Games with multiple medals.That is why the central story of India's sporting evolution should not simply be “India is winning more medals.” It is that India is becoming increasingly consistent at winning medals.India is not there yet. The Olympic record remains underwhelming. But the direction is unmistakable. The floor is rising.Aichi-Nagoya is the next testIndia will enter Aichi-Nagoya 2026 carrying the weight of its greatest Asian Games campaign, but the objective should not simply be to reproduce Hangzhou's 106.A 499-athlete contingent is heading to Japan, compared with 661 in Hangzhou. That difference makes a direct comparison difficult. The more meaningful test is whether India can sustain the performance level that has emerged over the last two decades.Can 50-plus remain the floor?Can 70-plus become the new expectation?Can more sports join the traditional medal pillars?Those are the questions that matter beyond the medal table.India may still be an under-achiever. But it is increasingly difficult to argue that the country is standing still.The medals are still not enough. The Olympic haul is still too modest. The Asian Games success still needs to be sustained. The conversion rate at the highest level still needs improvement. But the pattern has changed.From occasional Asian Games peaks to five consecutive 50-plus campaigns. From two historic multi-medal Olympics to five in a row. From a narrow collection of medal sports to a gradually expanding base.The peaks are getting higher. More importantly, the floor beneath them is rising.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mets’ Jared Young has concussion symptoms, CT scan negative after scary collision with Nolan McLean
articles.summary: Mets first baseman Jared Young was carted off the field in the sixth inning of Thursday night’s 3-0 loss to Philadelphia after he was knocked out when struck on the head by a knee of pitcher Nolan McLean as the two converged on Justin Crawford’s slow grounder.
articles.body: Mets first baseman Jared Young was carted off the field in the sixth inning of Thursday night’s 3-0 loss to Philadelphia after he was knocked out when struck on the head by a knee of pitcher Nolan McLean as the two converged on Justin Crawford’s slow grounder. New York manager Andy Green said a CT scan at a hospital was negative. Young had concussion symptoms and full use of his extremities, according to Green. “It was a terrifying moment on a baseball field,” Green said. “Took him a while to come to. It was a really scary collision.” With the Phillies ahead 1-0, McLean broke to first on contact and Young initially moved back toward the bag. McLean briefly paused, at which point Young reached for the ball with his right hand as he tried to keep a foot on the base. McLean resumed running then collided with Young’s head, tripping over the first baseman as Crawford crossed the bag. Young fell face first to the ground and was motionless. “It was scary to sit there and just know that he wasn’t with us in that moment,” Mets shortstop Francisco Lindor said. “He was just somewhere else.” Green and an athletic trainer immediately ran out from the dugout, and a cart was summoned. McLean put his hands on his knees and bent down as all the Mets on the field gathered near Young. Catcher Francisco Alvarez appeared to be praying and members of both teams looked on from the dugouts. Philadelphia’s Alec Bohm took a knee next to third base. When Young came to, Green said the first baseman asked: “What happened?” Young was immobilized on the cart and flashed a thumbs up before the cart disappeared behind the left-center field fence. “He’s had a CT scan. Results have come back negative,” Green said. “So in that sense it’s very positive. Still experiencing real concussion symptoms right now but has full use of his extremities and feels at this point in time like we’ve avoided the scariest outcomes.” Young, a 31-year-old in his first full big league season, has established himself as a regular first baseman by hitting .266 with nine homers and 39 RBIs in 103 games. He missed six weeks with a left knee injury. McLean was shaken by the collision. He remained in the game and threw a called third strike past Garrett Stubbs, ending the inning. “Probably should have made a better decision not even letting him get the next hitter but he was still strong enough to do it and got back out there and did it,” Green said. “I think the humanity hit him pretty hard right there.” McLean was removed by Green for reliever Tobias Myers at the start of the seventh. “Still was willing to go back out the next inning. Didn’t feel that was in his best interest at that point in time,” Green said.

articles.body: KOLKATA: The two top-ranked players at the North East Inter State Badminton Championships – Assam’s Ashmita Chaliha and H. Lalthazuala of Mizoram – shone on the opening day with identical one-sided wins for their teams in respective matches at Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Sports Complex in Shillong.While Chaliha, the world No. 41 and only Indian to win the Korea Masters, led Assam to a 3-0 win in a women’s team match against Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram’s former U17 national champion, Lalthazuala, was flawless in his team’s 3-0 victory over Tripura in their men’s team clash on Wednesday.It was, however, a disappointing start to the hosts’ campaign as Meghalaya lost their first matches in each of the four age categories in the team competition.But hosting the tournament after a decade and having more than 250 badminton players from across the northeast gathered in the Meghalaya capital for the four-day competition, the rise of grassroots talent across the region.In her message to the hosts’ shuttlers, who have not been able to gain the success of powerhouses like Assam and Mizoram, she said: “Enjoy what you articles.title: 'High chance we will bring home a medal': Yuvraj Sandhu confident ahead of Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Yuvraj Sandhu will be taking the long route to Japan. Back at 'sweet home' Chandigarh for five days, he has no time to rest after going thr.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Yuvraj Sandhu will be taking the long route to Japan. Back at 'sweet home' Chandigarh for five days, he has no time to rest after going through the rigours of the European Tour. It may be a quick reset in the lap of family, but at the nearby familiar course, there's practice and preparation with coach Gurbaaz Mann to deal with the long stretch ahead.Le Golf National awaits next week for the Open de France at the elegant-sounding Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines, under the suburban skies of Paris. There are boxes to tick, and a weekend wish, but the mind travels to the rolling hills of Kasugai Country Club, where the Asian Games competition starts on Sept 30."I played in Japan last year so I have a very fair idea how the golf courses are," he says. "We already have the course mapped out in detail, and the yardages. And I think playing on the DP World Tour has polished my game so I feel ready to tackle the course.""It's rained a lot there recently so the course will definitely be softer. We are expecting ideal weather. Besides, I'm pretty much accustomed to playing in such conditions, I've been playing in the rain four weeks out of the past eight," the 29-year-old adds.Japan golf connoisseur Jeev Milkha Singh has advised the Games-bound golfers to work on their short game, and Yuvraj doesn't need a reminder. "Last year, Jeev sir and I played together at International Series Japan, we stayed close by and had a few meals and he helped me a lot with understanding Japanese conditions in general, and, him being a legend in Japan, he's told me a few things about how to play the courses and I've taken his words to heart."And what about his rapport with the other members of the team, Saptak Talwar and Veer Ahlawat? "It's actually pretty good because we've played a lot of amateur golf together. We've also played junior golf together. Veer is a class senior to us, and he had a European Tour card last season. Saptak also plays on the second-tier Tour so we all have the experience. We are from the same age group so it makes it easier to talk about things around the course. I feel very comfortable going back to Japan, there's a high chance we will bring home a medal."Part of that confidence stems from the Euro grind, of course. "We play in 6 degrees when it's raining and the wind is howling at 40 kms/hr. There is a very big difference between just playing golf, and playing competitive golf in those battling conditions. So I think coping with that sort of mentality makes me more gritty, it makes me a more aggressive player when it comes to favourable conditions, probably like Japan."After winning seven PGTI tournaments in 2025, Yuvraj earned the pathway to the DP World Tour, and it has been a tough initiation. "When you go from a pool to an ocean, it makes a lot of difference. You are swimming with the fishes, and then suddenly you are swimming with the whales and sharks. So you got to grow and the transition takes time, but it's definitely all worth it. I will go to Q-School if things don't go my way. That's the reason I'm playing the sport. That's the dream," says the No. 202 in the Race to Dubai rankings."I've realized that it is important to address other things apart from swinging the club, be it the mental part or the rehab part. I've learned to be a better athlete, not just be a better golfer."A missed cut sometimes doesn't show your gains. "At the last tournament (Omega European Masters in Switzerland), I made seven-over on the first day, but in the second round, I shot 5-under. I played phenomenal golf. Not making the cut didn't really take a lot off my confidence, but somewhere, it does affect you. But your team helps you, and I have always believed in myself. Missing cuts are like making bogeys. You will make bogeys, you will make birdies. And the sooner you accept it, I think the better golfer you will be."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chess Olympiad Round 2: How Nihal Sarin saved India's day amid Gukesh's historic drop in rating points
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: The current world champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, was on Board 1 facing all the top-rated opponents during India's gold-clinching campaign in B.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The current world champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, was on Board 1 facing all the top-rated opponents during India's gold-clinching campaign in Budapest at the 2024 Chess Olympiad. Besides the team, Gukesh won an individual gold too, boosting his overall confidence ahead of the Championship challenge against China's Ding Liren. If that was the highest point of Gukesh's Olympiad journey, Round 2 of the 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad brought the lowest, as the 20-year-old Chennai grandmaster fell below 2700 rating after his draw against Indonesia's International Master (IM) Satria Duta Cahaya on Thursday in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.With Arjun Erigaisi taking a rest after his loss against Thai IM Prin Laohawirapap on the opening day of the tournament and Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa taking his designated Board 1 this time, Gukesh once again took Board 3 in India's match against Indonesia.The game itself, however, was a long, patient battle rather than a disaster.Playing black against a much lower-rated opponent, Gukesh went into a Sicilian setup and spent the middlegame manoeuvring, with his knights hopping back and forth, both kings tucked away, neither side finding a real breakthrough.Around the 40-move mark, pieces started coming off the board, and by the endgame Gukesh was left with a queen and knight against Cahaya's queen and knight, with roughly level chances.Needing a win to protect his rating and unable to find one, Gukesh eventually used his queen to give a string of checks around Cahaya's king, a "perpetual check", which forced the draw by repetition.It was a safe result, but not the kind expected from a reigning world champion against a 2412-rated opponent.Gukesh had started this Olympiad at 2703 and now sits at 2699.5, dropping below the 2700 mark for the first time since he first crossed it back in 2022.There is a general feeling that the Board 3 assignment could cut both ways for him. He won't run into the strongest opposition every round, but any slip against a lower-rated player carries outsized risk to his rating, exactly as it did on Thursday.With three of India's four boards ending in draws, it was Nihal Sarin who kept the team's campaign on track, beating Indonesia's Arif Abdul Hafiz. Even though for a large stretch of the game, that outcome looked far from certain.How Nihal Sarin saved India's dayPlaying white and the Sicilian Defence, Nihal castled queenside and launched a kingside attack with g4 and g5. However, Hafiz countered well, winning pawns and creating serious threats around Nihal’s king. After 22...Qxc2+, Black appeared to have taken control, while Nihal was also running dangerously low on time.The turning point came with 28.Rxc6+!, a bold rook sacrifice. Instead of trying to recover his material, Nihal chose to expose the black king. After 28...Kxc6, he continued with Qxe4+ and Qxb4, bringing his queen into the attack. A series of checks then forced the black king around the board, while Hafiz’s clock continued to fall.By 37.Nc5+, Black had no way out and resigned.It was a scrappy, double-edged fight rather than a clean demolition, but exactly the kind of gritty win India needed to avoid an upset.Elsewhere in the Indonesia match, Praggnanandhaa, back on Board 1 after Wednesday's rest day, drew with Susanto Megaranto, while Vidit Santosh Gujrathi also settled for a draw on Board 4 against Nayaka Budhidharma.With Nihal's win as the difference-maker, India closed out the match 2.5-1.5 to stay unbeaten through two rounds.Indian women's team registers comfortable win, opponents for Round 3 revealedWith Koneru Humpy taking a rest day, the 2025 Women's World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh made her first appearance in this edition of Women's Olympiad.Nevertheless, the women's team had a far more comfortable outing, brushing aside Finland 3.5-0.5. Vaishali Rameshbabu drew her game, but Divya, Vantika Agrawal and Savitha Shri all won to seal a dominant scoreline.India will look to keep the winning streak going on Friday, when the men's team takes on Italy, and the women face Greece.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Trouble in Japan! Indian athletes face accommodation, food and transport woes ahead of Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: Torrential rains battered this city last week, forcing evacuations, disrupting train services and even prompting the rescheduling of some Asia.
articles.body: NAGOYA: Torrential rains battered this city last week, forcing evacuations, disrupting train services and even prompting the rescheduling of some Asian Games events. Step into Nagoya today, though, and there is little sign any of it ever happened.As the city braces for the possibility of Typhoon Dujuan hitting the Aichi-Nagoya coast on Monday next, another storm has been brewing around the organising committee. Sustainability and cost-cutting may have been at the heart of the decision to do away with a traditional Games village, but the arrangement has instead triggered chaos and confusion for hundreds of athletes and officials.For many of the 17,000 athletes and officials arriving in the city, the wait at the airport to get their credentials validated and transport arranged has been at least three hours, with some stranded for as long as 14 hours. Already weary from their journey, they were left waiting at the airport, with food and basic arrangements becoming an issue.The problems, which began earlier in the week, continued on Thursday, two days before the Games officially open on Saturday. The confusion did not end at the airport. Athletes arriving at their accommodation were faced with uncertainty over room allocation, with even the hosts caught up in the mess. A section of the Japanese contingent had to seek alternative arrangements after men and women were allotted shared rooms. Indian Olympic Association officials too faced room-allocation issues and were left without accommodation before alternative arrangements were eventually made. Space has emerged as another concern. While compact accommodation is hardly unfamiliar in Japan, the cramped quarters have taken several contingents by surprise. The Costa Serena cruise ship, docked at Kinjo Pier, is housing around 4,000 athletes.Japan’s deputy chef de mission Hisashi Mizutori acknowledged the problems at a press conference on Thursday. “Since the cruise ship village opened, athletes have been arriving and going through the entry procedures. However, the process took a significant amount of time due to issues with activation of their credentials,” he said.The container-style huts, built with an eye on future use as disaster evacuation facilities, have also come under scrutiny. “There is no space to store luggage and we are not here for few days but three weeks, so it’s a challenge in the containers. The ones built for acclimatisation back home by Sports Authority of India were much bigger,” rued an IOA official, an Asian Games veteran. Food has been another source of discontent. While some contingents found fare difficult to adapt, others complained that quantities were inadequate and were forced to eat outside.Travel woes for shootersLogistical problems continued to hit contingents on Thursday. With venues spread across the region and accommodation located some distance away, athletes have been spending hours on the road and, in some cases, missing scheduled training slots. The Indian shooting team was among those affected. The journey from their accommodation to the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery was expected to take around 75 minutes. Instead, the team took more than two hours to reach the venue after waiting nearly three hours for transport to arrive.By then, the Indians had missed their allotted practice slot and had to wait for other teams to finish before getting their turn. Away from the chaos, Nagoya is preparing to welcome the Asian Games back to Japan after a 32-year gap. The industrial and automotive hub is decked out in Games posters and buntings, with trains, subways and streets carrying the colours of the event.Amid the organisational troubles, locals have stepped up. Impromptu volunteers are helping athletes and visitors to navigate the sprawling venues, decipher an unfamiliar language and even find foodGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Despite loss, India’s teqball story only just beginning
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Nagoya: India’s Asian Games journey began in rather muted fashion at the Higashi Sports Centre here at 4:06 pm. There was no fanfare and barely any in.
articles.body: Nagoya: India’s Asian Games journey began in rather muted fashion at the Higashi Sports Centre here at 4:06 pm. There was no fanfare and barely any indication that history was being made. A volunteer holding a placard was the only sign that an Asian Games event was under way.The sport was teqball — a little-known combination of football and table tennis — and India’s men’s doubles pair of Declan Gonsalves and Mohamed Anas went down fighting 10-12, 8-12 to Vietnam and 4-12, 7-12 to South Korea.Their campaign ended, but for India’s small community of about 180 teqball athletes, the day marked the beginning of something bigger. One of six sports making its Asian Games debut, teqball is played on a curved table resembling a table-tennis table. The sport originated in Hungary and is only 12 years old. In India, it has been around for barely four years.That hasn’t stopped a small band of ‘teqers’ from chasing their passion.On Thursday, six Indians in the stands cheered Gonsalves and Anas. Among them were India’s deputy chef de mission and former shooting stalwart Anjali Bhagwat, and Declan’s parents Derek and Deborah Gonsalves, who had flown in from Mumbai to witness a slice of history.Anas will get another opportunity when he teams up with Quimcy Dsouza in the mixed doubles. Quimcy will also compete in the women’s singles.For the first generation of Indian teqers, the last four years have involved as much explaining as playing.“All the four years I have been playing the sport, I’ve only been explaining what it is. But the Asian Games is a huge opportunity for us,” said Bengaluru-based Quimcy, who quit her job in Mumbai and moved to the city to set up a teqball facility.She was drawn to the sport after watching videos of former Brazil football star Ronaldinho playing it on social media.“I started playing the sport around the time the last Asian Games was held. Back then, if somebody told me I would be playing in the Asian Games this year, I wouldn’t have believed it. This is a dream come true,” said Quimcy, one of a group of self-taught athletes who have now taken on coaching roles as well.Nihar Shah, technical director of Teqball India, believes the sport is beginning to find a foothold, particularly in the Northeast, where several players have a background in sepaktakraw.“While it’s still new, there has been a lot of interest in it lately. We hope the Asian Games appearance of the three athletes gives it a further push,” Shah said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rowers head into Asian Games hoping to peak when it matters most
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Fewer sport test the limits of human endurance, power and stamina as rowing does. A marathoner might expend around 3,000 kilocalories over a 42.2km co.
articles.body: Fewer sport test the limits of human endurance, power and stamina as rowing does. A marathoner might expend around 3,000 kilocalories over a 42.2km course, but he or she does so at a sub-optimal level, meaning the rate of burn is about 13 kilocalories per minute.In comparison, an oarsman may require only around 140 kilocalories to complete a 2km race lasting 5.5 to 7.5 minutes. The total energy demand may be far lower, but the intensity is much higher, reaching about 20 kilocalories per minute.While the distance runner has to tap into his reserves over a sustained period for a prolonged effort, the rower draws on 85 per cent of his muscles with each stroke, as opposed to 50 percent in the case of running. Then you add the unpredictable: the elements.The key element, though, is the human in the boat.The Indian team’s preparation in this Asian Games cycle has received a large dose of sports science, thanks to the arrival of Australian Antony Patterson at the Army Rowing Node. Conversations are peppered with phrases like heart rate, prognostic percentage and living document. The women rowers, meanwhile, have found corporate backing in recent years.Under Patterson, there has also been a fundamental shift in selecting team combinations, perhaps necessitated by the new rule that countries can compete in only 10 events. So, whereas in the past top rowers entered their strongest events, this time events with maximum chance of winning a medal have been identified and combinations decided accordingly.But while the preparation has been science-driven and meticulous, a positive dope test and the ministry’s decision to axe two women’s teams had dented the squad’s morale. A fourth-place finish in the lightweight double scull at last month’s World Championships and a recent mind-training session in Pune seems to have revived their confidence.Time, then, for India’s rowers to translate meticulous preparation into medals.# Riding the tide of hopeHaving won three medals (one silver and two bronze) in each of the past two editions of the Asian Games, Indian sailors will be looking to add to their tally when they set out on the water in Gamagori City.Vishnu Saravanan (ILCA-7), Nethra Kumanan (ILCA-6), Harshita Tomar (49erFX) and debutant Manu Francis (49er) give India a chance to improve on its best-ever showing at the continental event.India’s main rivals are expected to be China, hosts Japan and Malaysia.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: El periodista reivindica al argentino como uno de los favoritos al galardón tras conquistar otro título con el Inter de Miami
articles.body: La carrera por el Balón de Oro tiene varios nombres sobre la mesa, pero David Sánchez ha querido añadir uno que conoce perfectamente lo que significa levantar el galardón: Leo Messi. El periodista defendió en La Tribu la candidatura del argentino después de conquistar un nuevo título con el Inter de Miami. Mientras buena parte del debate gira alrededor de Lamine Yamal y Kylian Mbappé, David Sánchez puso el foco en el futbolista con más Balones de Oro: "Que nadie olvide que el que más Balones de Oro tiene ha vuelto a rendir a un nivel parecido a las temporadas en las cuales ganó ese Balón de Oro". David Sánchez destacó también el palmarés de Messi después de su último éxito con el Inter de Miami. "Otro título, hace 24 horas, levantó Leo Messi con su equipo, el Inter de Miami. Un palmarés espectacular. No hay jugador en el mundo que haya ganado más títulos que el delantero argentino", señaló. Un nuevo trofeo que, para el periodista, refuerza los argumentos del argentino en la carrera por el premio individual. David Sánchez fue contundente al colocar a Messi entre los principales aspirantes: "Es para mí un firme candidato a levantar un nuevo Balón de Oro, por lo que viene haciendo en las últimas temporadas". El periodista incidió especialmente en el rendimiento de Messi en el Mundial y lo comparó directamente con otros candidatos al Balón de Oro. "Con 39 años de edad, fue el mejor jugador del Mundial. No marcó tantos goles como Kylian Mbappé, pero jugó mucho mejor que Kylian Mbappé, que Kane o que Lamine Yamal", afirmó. David Sánchez cerró su intervención dejando clara su apuesta por la candidatura del argentino: "Para mí, Leo Messi está entre los favoritos para ganar un nuevo Balón de Oro".

articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: India’s Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza produced a stunning comeback against Japan’s top-seeded Yuina Sakamoto before following it up with another co.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza produced a stunning comeback against Japan’s top-seeded Yuina Sakamoto before following it up with another convincing victory to march into the women’s singles semifinals in Teqball at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Friday.Making her Asian Games debut in a sport appearing at the continental Games for the first time, the Indian showed remarkable composure under pressure at the Nagoya City Higashi Sports Center. She recovered from losing the opening game against Sakamoto to prevail 2-1 in a hard-fought contest.Dsouza lost the first game 10-12 but responded brilliantly, edging the Japanese player 12-11 in the second before sealing the match 13-11 in the decider.She then carried that momentum into her second group match, defeating Cambodia’s Koemyean DY 2-0. Dsouza won the opening game 12-9 before closing out the contest 12-7 to finish top of her group and earn a direct berth in the semifinals.One win away from historic medalThe result puts Dsouza just one victory away from securing a historic medal for India in Teqball.She will face Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in Saturday’s semifinal. A victory would guarantee Dsouza a place on the podium, while a defeat would give her another opportunity in the bronze-medal match against the loser of the other semifinal between Myanmar’s Wai Khin Hin and Lebanon’s Kamar Dandal.For Dsouza, the achievement is particularly significant as Teqball makes its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026. The sport, which originated in Hungary, combines elements of football with a curved table and is played in singles, doubles and mixed doubles.Mixed doubles challenge awaitsDsouza’s busy day also included the mixed doubles event, where she partnered Mohamed Anas Imran Beg. The Indian pair began their campaign with a win over the Philippines’ Jhoana Abulencia and Prince Agustin.They were scheduled to face Cambodia, Thailand and Kuwait in the remainder of their group-stage campaign.India’s other Teqball representatives, Beg and Declan Marshall Gonsalves, had earlier endured a difficult start in the men’s doubles, losing both their group matches.
