articles.title: Nueve de cada diez conductores suspenderían hoy el examen teórico si tuvieran que repetirlo
articles.standfirst: El ultimo estudio de la Fundación Línea Directa revela que suspenderían el teórico el 91,9% de los conductores españoles, unos 26 millones de personas
articles.summary: El ultimo estudio de la Fundación Línea Directa revela que suspenderían el teórico el 91,9% de los conductores españoles, unos 26 millones de personas
articles.body: Nueve de cada diez conductores españoles suspenderían hoy el examen teórico si tuvieran que volver a presentarse. Así lo revela un estudio de la Fundación Línea Directa, elaborado en colaboración con Fesvial y Etrasa, que ha sometido a 1.700 conductores de toda la geografía española a una prueba que reproduce con fidelidad el examen oficial. El trabajo de campo se realizó entre el 3 y el 10 de agosto de 2026, y sus resultados, según reconoce la propia fundación, buscan concienciar a los automovilistas de la necesidad de seguir formándose una vez obtenido el carné. La DGT contabiliza en la actualidad más de 28 millones de conductores en España, en torno al 58% de la población total. Obtener el permiso ya resulta exigente de entrada. De hecho, en 2024 (último año de los que se tienen datos disponibles) se realizaron cerca de de 1,05 millones de pruebas teóricas y casi la mitad, el 49% en concreto, terminó en suspenso. El 91,9% de los conductores que acabarían suspendiendo supone que 26 millones de conductores de nuestro país no estarían en condiciones de conducir al haber cometido más de tres fallos. Por lo menos, en cuanto a la teoría se refiere. Dentro de este grupo de suspensos, la gran mayoría, el 75,4%, comete entre 4 y 10 errores, mientras que el 16,5% supera la decena de fallos, un porcentaje que representa a 4,7 millones de conductores, el doble de quienes aprobarían. Las preguntas sobre motocicletas y ciclomotores concentran el mayor número de fallos, con un 62,8% de errores entre los participantes. Le siguen las cuestiones de señalización vertical, horizontal y luminosa, con un 30%, y la normativa vial, que incluye permisos, velocidades máximas y prohibiciones de circulación, con un 26,8%. La edad también juega en contra del aprobado. El 89,8% de los conductores de 18 a 30 años suspendería el examen, un porcentaje que sube al 92,2% entre quienes tienen de 44 a 55 años y que alcanza el 94,5% entre los mayores de 55. Casi el 82% de los conductores obtuvo el carné hace más de una década, y solo en el último año se crearon o actualizaron unas 130 señales de tráfico, un dato que ayuda a entender por qué la Fundación Línea Directa apunta al paso del tiempo, la falta de reciclaje y los cambios normativos como posibles explicaciones, aunque lo plantea como probabilidad y no como certeza. El propio estudio introduce, sin embargo, un matiz importante: una cosa es recordar bien las normas y otra muy distinta es conducir con seguridad en la carretera. Según los datos oficiales de la DGT recogidos en la base de accidentes ARENA, los conductores con más de 10 años de carné, casi el 82% del censo total, solo representan el 64,6% de los implicados en accidentes con víctimas. Sin embargo, los conductores noveles, con 0 o 1 año de antigüedad, siguen el patrón inverso, suponen apenas el 4% del censo pero acumulan el 7,6% de los implicados en ese tipo de siniestros, casi el doble de lo que le correspondería por su peso demográfico. Mar Garre, directora general de la Fundación Línea Directa, asegura que "los resultados del test demuestran que aprobar el carné no puede ser el punto final de la formación vial. Las normas cambian, aparecen nuevas formas de movilidad y, con el paso del tiempo, muchos conocimientos se olvidan. Resulta imprescindible, por tanto, consolidar una cultura de actualización y aprendizaje continuo que nos permita mantener nuestros conocimientos al día que contribuya a una conducción más segura". En cuanto a Comunidades Autónomas, ninguna se libra de un resultado negativo y en todas ellas las cifras son parecidas. Canarias, con un 95,9% de suspensos, encabeza la clasificación, seguida de Extremadura (95,7%), Aragón (94,8%), la Región de Murcia (94,7%), la Comunidad Valenciana (94,5%) y La Rioja (94,5%). Por debajo de esas cifras se sitúan Castilla-La Mancha (93,8%), la Comunidad de Madrid (93%), Baleares (92,5%), Navarra (92,5%), Cantabria (92,4%), Castilla y León (91,8%) y el País Vasco (91,8%), todas ellas próximas a la media nacional del 91,9%. Cierran la tabla, con los porcentajes más bajos, aunque elevados en términos absolutos, Andalucía (90%), Cataluña (89,8%), Asturias (88,3%) y Galicia (87,1%), la única comunidad que baja del 90%. La clave que subyace tras estos números reside en que el 77% de los conductores reconoce no haber vuelto a recibir formación después de aprobar el permiso, y otro 10% dice haber accedido solo a información puntual, sin llegar a completar un curso reglado. Pese a ese vacío, el 84% de los españoles considera necesario reciclar sus conocimientos de conducción, aunque no hay consenso sobre cómo hacerlo: un 32% propone repetirlo cada 10 años, mientras un 39% plantea exigirlo a partir de una determinada edad. Preguntados por los contenidos que consideran más urgentes, los conductores señalan la actualización de las normas de tráfico (67%) y la interpretación de señales (32%). En el ámbito práctico, las prioridades pasan por la reacción ante imprevistos y emergencias (41%) y la conducción con fenómenos meteorológicos adversos (35%). Sobre las pruebas para obtener el carné, 7 de cada 10 españoles consideran adecuado el nivel de dificultad del examen práctico, que un 53% ve más sencillo que el teórico. Con todo, el 28% de los conductores admite que, tras aprobar, no se sentía preparado para circular con seguridad, y a la hora de explicar los suspensos, los nervios y la presión (62%) superan con claridad a la falta de preparación (26%) como causa principal. El coste añade otra capa de preocupación, 4 de cada 5 conductores lo consideran un lujo, ya que el desembolso total puede superar los 1.000 euros si se realizan 20 clases prácticas.

articles.title: 'Nothing against sportsman spirit': Pakistan explain decision to boycott Israel at Chess Olympiad
articles.summary: Chess News: Pakistan refused to play Israel in the opening round of the 46th FIDE World Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Wednesday, handing Israel a 4-.
articles.body: Pakistan refused to play Israel in the opening round of the 46th FIDE World Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Wednesday, handing Israel a 4-0 win by walkover.Pakistan did not field any player for the scheduled match, leaving all four boards unplayed.The Chess Federation of Pakistan (CFP) said the decision followed the Pakistani government's policy towards Israel and was also meant to show solidarity with Palestinians.Pakistan cites state policyGauhar Iqbal, Secretary General of the Pakistan Chess Federation, explained that the decision was based on Pakistan's official position and not on the players involved."It was very obvious that when we do not recognize a state,how can we play or how can we get engaged with that state? It's a state policy, and we have to follow the state as we are here to represent Pakistan, and we have to follow the policies of Pakistan," Gauhar Iqbal, Secretary General of Pakistan Chess Federation, told ChessBase India, explaining why Pakistan chose against taking on Israel in Round 1 of the Chess Olympiad 2026"So we are here. It is nothing against any player. It is nothing against any sportsman spirit. It's against the state's policy, and we have followed that."Pakistan to continue international participationCFP President Syed Zeeshan Naqvi also said the boycott was intended to express support for the Palestinian people. "We have boycotted the match to express solidarity with the Palestinian people," Naqvi said.Naqvi said Pakistan would continue to participate in international sporting events while following the government's official position on Israel.The Pakistan-Israel match was part of the opening round of the biennial Chess Olympiad. Since Pakistan did not take part, Israel received a 4-0 victory without a single move being played.The Chess Olympiad is being held in Samarkand from September 15 to 27, with separate open and women's competitions.More than 390 teams are taking part across the two sections. The event brings together national teams from around the world and is one of the biggest tournaments on the international chess calendar.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India’s flag bearers revealed: Manu Bhaker, Tajinderpal Singh Toor to lead contingent at Asian Games opening ceremony
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and two-time defending Asian Games shot put champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor will carry the Indian flag.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and two-time defending Asian Games shot put champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor will carry the Indian flag at the opening ceremony of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Saturday, giving the country two champions from different generations of Indian sport to lead the contingent into the continental Games.India’s Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav confirmed Bhaker’s selection on Friday, while the Athletics Federation of India later announced Toor as the second flag-bearer.“Manu Bhaker will be one of the flag-bearers,” Yadav said.Bhaker arrives in Nagoya with a landmark Olympic achievement behind her. At the Paris Olympics in 2024, the shooter became the first athlete from independent India to win two medals in a single edition of the Games.She won bronze in the women’s 10m air pistol and followed it with another bronze in the mixed team 10m air pistol event alongside Sarabjot Singh, becoming one of the standout Indian performers at the Paris Games.Toor brings Asian Games pedigreeToor, meanwhile, will lead India into the opening ceremony with his own strong Asian Games record.The shot putter is a two-time defending champion, having won gold at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games before retaining his title at Hangzhou in 2023. He will now attempt to extend that run in Aichi-Nagoya.The 31-year-old heads an Indian athletics contingent that will be aiming to maintain the sport's strong contribution to the country's medal tally. Toor is among the Indian athletes expected to challenge for a podium finish despite entering the Games amid questions over his current form.The opening ceremony is scheduled for Saturday, September 19, at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, officially marking the start of the 20th Asian Games.Opening ceremony follows logistical concernsThe flag-bearers were announced on a day when the Indian contingent was also caught up in an organisational disruption.India’s traditional team welcome and flag-hoisting ceremony at Nagoya Port Garden Pier was delayed and then abruptly halted after organisers cited unspecified “trouble” involving a team. India’s deputy Chef de Missions A Sharath Kamal, Lijo David Thottan, Alaknanda Ashok and Anjali Bhagwat were present for the ceremony.The disruption came amid wider concerns over accommodation, transport and credentialing arrangements in the lead-up to the Games. Organisers have opted against a conventional athletes’ village, instead using container-style accommodation, hotels and a docked cruise ship to house participants.Despite the off-field challenges, India’s sporting campaign is already underway, with athletes competing across disciplines ahead of Saturday’s formal opening. The country has sent a 503-member contingent to Aichi-Nagoya.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Another slow start offensively hurts Lions: 'We stalled out early'
articles.summary: Jared Goff says the Lions must find urgency after a slow start put them in a 21-0 hole that they couldn't climb out of against the Bills.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — At the opening of Highmark Stadium, the new home of the Buffalo Bills , most fans were in their seats and ready to go with more than 20 minutes until game time.

Most players from the Detroit Lions , however, didn't show up until the end of the first quarter.

Quarterback Jared Goff was under duress in critical situations on the first two drives, which lasted a combined seven plays and netted negative-1 yard. Add in some fast-and-furious work from the Bills' offense, and the Lions were behind the eight ball before the smoke even cleared from the pregame fireworks in a 41-31 loss on Thursday, Sept. 17.

Goff said the team needs to have more "urgency early on." The Lions have scored 17 points in the first half and 45 points in the second half and overtime through their first two games. Detroit overcame it in the opener against New Orleans, a 31-30 overtime win , but couldn't afford the early stumbles against Buffalo in a game that was shaping up to be a shootout from jump.

"I think for the last two games, really, we've had good moments, but I think we need to really understand that we need to start good," Goff said. "We need to start on that momentum and ignite some of those plays in the first drive and not allow ourselves to get in these holes."

On the first drive, running back Jahmyr Gibbs was stuffed for no gain on second-and-8 and Goff was sacked on third-and-long, ending the series with a three-and-out.

On their second drive, Gibbs gained 16 yards and got the offense to second-and-1 the next play, but Goff was sacked on second down to make it third-and-11. Then backup center Juice Scruggs snapped the ball over Goff's head, ending the series after four plays.

Last week against the Saints, Detroit punted on four of its first six drives and fumbled on another.

Against a Bills offense that put up 36 points against the vaunted Houston Texans defense a week prior, their early stumbles were a death sentence on Thursday night. The Lions trailed 21-0 with 11:48 to go in the second quarter and were down 27-10 as they entered the locker room at halftime.

"We knew we needed to score some points. We stalled out early in that game. That got us early," Lions coach Dan Campbell said. "You're down three scores, and really, we haven't done anything offensively. So a lot of that help needed to come there (on offense), to be able to answer back. So, we fell short there."

As the Lions looked to make it a one-score game with less than two minutes left in the first half, Scruggs was called for a false start on third-and-1 near midfield and Goff was then sacked on third-and-5, ending the series. The Lions committed three false start penalties, including two on Larry Borom, who was starting in place of Blake Miller.

"We got to handle it better, and some of those penalties killed us, man, it really did," Goff said.

The Lions will have extra time to diagnose the problems behind their slow starts before they take the field against the New York Jets on Sunday, Sept. 27. Goff said he's looking forward to working on "consistency."

"And again, like, finding a way to be very intentional about starting fast. I think both games, like I said, we have good moments, we've really had good second halves in both games, but being intentional about, 'Hey, this game starts in the first quarter, let's go,'" Goff said.

Plenty will be written and talked about this Lions' defense, and rightfully so. But the strength of this team has always been its offense, and without better starts, the Lions don't stand a chance against the league's best.

articles.title: Houston Astros 6-Year Player Suffers Season-Ending Injury Before Braves Series
articles.summary: A Houston Astros player who has played six seasons for the club suffered a season-ending injury before the Braves series. The post Houston Astros 6-Year Play...
articles.body:
The Houston Astros are set to begin a three-game series against the Atlanta Braves at Daikin Park in Houston on Friday night.

Before the Braves series, an Astros player who has played six seasons for the team reportedly suffered a season-ending injury.

Houston Astros 6-Year Player Suffers Brutal Injury Before Braves Series

Astros outfielder is out for the remainder of the season after fouling a ball off his left kneecap in a minor-league game, according to MLB.com's Brian McTaggart.

McTaggart wrote on X : Jake Meyers ' season ended Sept. 11 at Triple-A Sugar Land when he fouled a ball off his left knee cap. He posted a .592 OPS in 39 Minor League games, .594 in 57 games with the Astros.

Meyers, 30, hit .213/.268/.326 with three home runs and 11 RBI over 57 games with Houston this season.

The outfielder slashed .231/.301/.338 with two homers and 13 RBI at the Triple-A level this year.

The Astros selected Meyers in the 13th round (No. 391 overall) of the 2017 MLB Draft out of the University of Nebraska.

Meyers made his MLB debut with Houston in 2021.

Meyers has appeared in 522 games with the Astros over the past six seasons.

During that span, Meyers hit .241/.303/.367 with 36 home runs and 172 RBI.

Meyers has recorded innings at all three outfield positions in the majors but is mainly a center fielder.

Meyers has three hits in 12 postseason at-bats. He won a World Series with Houston in 2022.

Next year will be Meyers' final year of arbitration. He is being paid $3.55 million this season. Throughout his career, Meyers has made $8,260,092.

Friday's game between the Astros and Braves is scheduled to begin at 7:10 p.m. CDT. Fans can watch on the Space City Home Network.

The Indianapolis Colts released their Thursday injury report for Week 2 of the NFL season against the Kansas City Chiefs .

Giddens however can't afford to miss time with injury as it could end up costing him his roster spot.

Linebacker Austin Ajake (hamstring) was a full participant at practice. Shake looks like he should be healthy enough to contribute on Sunday. Wide receiver Keenan Allen )rest) was a full participant at practice. Allen was a full go after taking Wednesday off with a scheduled rest day.

articles.title: ‘He’s Gonna Show Them’ — Travis Hunter Sends a Defiant Warning on Behalf of Shedeur Sanders With Browns QB Waiting in the Wings
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are sticking with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback, at least for the time being. After a competition with Shedeur Sanders, t...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are sticking with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback, at least for the time being. After a competition with Shedeur Sanders , the three-time Pro Bowler walked away with the QB1 role.

But the early returns have been far from stellar. After a brutal Week 1 performance, fans are already clamoring for a switch. Now, the second-year quarterback is getting a vote of confidence from his former teammate, Travis Hunter .

Travis Hunter Believes Shedeur Sanders Is the Better Choice for the Browns

New Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken split first-team reps between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders as they competed for the starting quarterback role. However, with the former Houston Texans star running a more stable operation, Monken gave him the job.

That decision wasn't popular with the Browns fan base, who were already raining down boos at Watson during the preseason. He fired back at fans in his postgame press conference but later apologized for his comments.

With a dud in Week 1, the demand for Sanders to take over the starting role has been intense. And Hunter, who played alongside Sanders for the Colorado Buffaloes and won the Heisman Trophy with him at quarterback, gave him his approval.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"I wish he was playing too," Hunter said before the Week 1 game when the Jacksonville Jaguars blew out the Browns 34-10. "It's all good, though. He's gonna get his chance. When he gets his chance again, he's gonna show them. He's gonna show them why."

In Week 1, Watson threw for 205 yards and a touchdown while throwing an interception on Cleveland's opening drive. Moreover, the Jaguars built a 31-0 lead before the Browns scored their first points.

Add in some operational issues, and the vitriol against the veteran quarterback was intense. Now, the Browns face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2 before their home opener the following week.

If Watson cannot turn things around quickly, he could walk into an extremely hostile environment in Week 3. That could increase pressure on the Browns to make a change and put Sanders back into the starting role.

Last year, after both Joe Flacco and Dillon Gabriel had time under center, Sanders finally got his chance and started the final seven games.

He finished the 2025 season with 1,400 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions, ranking 37th among 38 qualifying quarterbacks in PFN's Quarterback Impact Metrics.

But the Browns might gain more from developing the younger Sanders than from sticking with Watson through the final season of his contract.

articles.title: Red Sox's Willson Contreras admits hand was 'numb' after hit by pitch in Rangers game
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox entered their 2025 Wild Card Series versus the New York Yankees with injuries to key players, and both the team and fan base desperately w...
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox entered their 2025 Wild Card Series versus the New York Yankees with injuries to key players, and both the team and fan base desperately want to avoid that scenario this year. Therefore, concern was high when Willson Contreras got hit in the hand with a pitch during the eighth inning of Thursday's game versus the Texas Rangers . Trevor Story lifted Boston to a 4-3 lead and eventual win a few minutes later, and then the injured first baseman received big news. There is no fracture.

Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy revealed that the X-rays were negative, but he is dealing with a bruise and swelling. The team is taking a day-by-day approach with nine regular season games left to play. Contreras himself was thinking the worst .

"Sore. Painful. My hand was numb for like five minutes," the four-time All-Star said, per MassLive.com's Chris Cotillo. "That was the reason I came out of the game. I have fractured, before, the same hand. It felt like a fracture. Thankfully, it's not a fracture on the top of the bone. I'm just frustrated."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Contreras has already expressed exasperation over getting drilled with pitches, and this latest instance is especially brutal given the time of the year. He leads the Red Sox with 27 home runs, 81 RBIs, a .387 on-base percentage, .518 slugging percentage and .905 OPS, so his postseason availability is obviously crucial. The early diagnosis seems promising, but Boston's medical staff has whiffed on its injury timelines before.

A summer shift to small-ball tactics propelled this previously flat-lining ballclub firmly into playoff contention, but Willson Contreras remains the Sox's most complete hitter. He just returned from the injured list after battling a hamstring strain. Boston's bad luck continues.

This squad already got off the mat once, however. Perhaps it can survive another heavy blow. If nothing else, Thursday's heroic comeback over the Rangers brings the Red Sox (83-70) one win closer to clinching a second straight playoff berth. The magic number is down to three.

articles.title: Sporting director reveals he was shocked by one of Liverpool’s summer signings
articles.summary: Lucca Brughmans to Liverpool: Why the Fee Still Raises Questions Despite Genk’s ExcitementLiverpool’s summer business has already had a visible impact on lif...
articles.body:
Lucca Brughmans to Liverpool : Why the Fee Still Raises Questions Despite Genk's Excitement

Liverpool's summer business has already had a visible impact on life at Anfield, with several arrivals settling quickly under Andoni Iraola . Yet one deal continues to stand apart from the rest, and fresh comments from Genk have only sharpened the focus on it.

According to Dimitri De Conde via Sport Witness , the Belgian club themselves did not foresee the speed or scale of Liverpool's move for teenage goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans. That admission is revealing. It points to a transfer that appears to have accelerated rapidly late in the window, and one that may have carried a premium because of the timing as much as the player's potential.

Liverpool transfer strategy under scrutiny

There is no great mystery around Liverpool's wider recruitment model. The club have long tried to balance immediate improvement with long-term planning, and that remained the case this summer. Some additions were made for the first team, others with development in mind. Brughmans clearly belongs in the second category.

That is where the debate begins. Liverpool were linked with Brughmans as a possible second-choice goalkeeper, but the final outcome saw him return to Genk on loan. From a development perspective, that is understandable. For an 18-year-old goalkeeper, regular football in a familiar environment can be worth more than a season of training and waiting around at a major Premier League club.

From a financial perspective, though, it invites a different line of questioning. If the player was not expected to contribute immediately, and if he was always likely to stay in Belgium for another year, Liverpool's willingness to pay such a sizeable fee looks unusual.

Genk reaction says plenty about Brughmans fee

De Conde's account of the move underlines just how quickly events unfolded. He said, "I knew he was on the radar of top clubs." He added, "He was one of the lads we hoped to get a handsome fee for at some point, to ensure the club's survival. But for it to happen that quickly. And for that amount, I never saw that coming."

That is a striking assessment from the selling club's own sporting director. It suggests Liverpool moved decisively and left little room for drawn-out negotiation. De Conde continued, "People saying 'It's fantastic what De Conde achieved with his experience regarding Lucca's transfer!' Sorry, but that's not the case." He then explained, "In the end, I got a call from his agency at 11am on a Sunday, two days before the English transfer window closed. Liverpool is serious. 'This is the offer.' And the very next morning, Lucca was on a plane to Liverpool. I do take credit for the fact that we, as a club, chose that path."

For Liverpool, that sort of speed can be viewed in two ways. It can reflect conviction, with the recruitment team determined to secure a goalkeeper they rated highly. Equally, it can create the impression of a market opportunity pursued at a cost beyond what might have been necessary earlier in the process.

There is no doubt Brughmans is regarded as a talented young goalkeeper. Liverpool will have done extensive background work on his profile, pathway and ceiling before sanctioning the move. Clubs at this level do not commit notable sums on young players without strong internal backing.

Still, fees shape expectations. When a teenager arrives for a substantial amount, the scrutiny follows quickly, whether he is playing at Anfield or developing elsewhere. For a goalkeeper, that pressure can be even more pronounced given the nature of the position and the slower developmental curve attached to it.

At this stage, the move feels less like a clear overpayment and more like a high-cost projection. That distinction matters. Liverpool may yet be proved right if Brughmans develops into a first-team goalkeeper of elite level. Until then, the Genk reaction serves as a reminder that this was a deal which surprised even those benefiting from it.

From a hopeful Liverpool supporter's perspective, there is still plenty of room for optimism here. The fee looks high, yes, and when even Genk seem surprised by it, fans are always going to ask questions. That is perfectly fair. Liverpool supporters have seen enough transfer windows to know when a deal feels a little left-field.

But there is another side to it. Goalkeepers develop differently, and if the club genuinely believe Lucca Brughmans has top-level potential, then paying a bit more now could look smart in a few years. Liverpool have clearly decided that this is a player worth securing before his value rises further or before rival clubs move more aggressively.

The loan back to Genk also feels sensible. Throwing an 18-year-old goalkeeper straight into the pressure of being around the first team at Anfield might not have been ideal. Letting him grow, play and mature in Belgium could be exactly what he needs before taking the next step.

Supporters will naturally compare the fee with other goalkeepers and wonder whether the club could have landed him for less. That may be true. Still, if Brughmans turns into Liverpool's long-term answer in goal, nobody will care much about the extra few million pounds. For now, it is a gamble, but one that fans can still talk themselves into believing will pay off.

articles.title: Eagles news: Jordan Mailata dismisses Jeffery Simmons' Jalen Hurts slander
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are gearing up for their clash against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on Sunday. The Eagles are coming off a narrow escape ag...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are gearing up for their clash against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on Sunday. The Eagles are coming off a narrow escape against the Washington Commanders , 24-22, in Week 1.

Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts dusted off a sluggish start and made big plays in the fourth quarter to complete the hard-earned win.

Ahead of their meeting, Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said they know how to stop Hurts.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"We just need to make Jalen Hurts be a QB. Stop his runs, make sure Hurts doesn't get out of the pocket and make plays," said Simmons.

When told about Simmons' claim, Eagles offensive tackle Jordan Mailata brushed it off , while also directly shading the media.

"I don't pay attention to that stuff. That's clickbait stuff. That's what you guys get paid for," said Mailata, as quoted by The Athletic's Zach Berman.

"I only care about everyone in this locker room. This locker room is all I give a damn about. I don't care what you guys say about this locker room. I don't care what any other locker room says about this locker room. This is my focus."

Hurts went 14-of-25 for 203 yards, three touchdowns, and zero interceptions against the Commanders. He also ran for 46 yards on seven carries.

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni touted Hurts' dual-threat ability .

"One of the things that makes Jalen such a special quarterback is that he can do it through the air. He can do it running the show. He can do it with his legs when he needs to make plays," said Sirianni in a report from the Associated Press.

Philadelphia stuffed Washington's two-point attempt in the final minute to preserve the two-point victory.

articles.title: How will Barcelona line up against Sevilla?
articles.summary: Hansi Flick’s possible XI for Saturday’s clash
articles.body:
Barcelona look to continue their history-making perfect start to the season and make it seven wins out of seven in La Liga as the leaders travel to the Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán for a tough road game against Sevilla.

Hansi Flick has done a good job of rotating his squad with lineup choices and substitutions at the start of the season, and he'll do it once again this weekend.

There will have to be one enforced change at the back as Joan Garcia will miss the trip to Seville with a knee issue, and Wojciech Szczesny is expected to start in goal despite his error against Racing Santander in midweek.

The back four could also see changes with Jules Kounde starting against his former club ahead of Eric Garcia at right-back and Xavi Espart returning at left-back after getting a rest in midweek.

Pau Cubarsí was also rested against Racing and will start at center-back alongside Gerard Martín , with Andreas Christensen getting the night off in this one.

Flick has been watchful of Rodri and Pedri 's minutes at the start of the season so they are always available to start, and they are expected in the lineup on Saturday after playing only an hour in midweek. Fermín López got a full 90-minute rest against Racing and is expected back in the lineup for this one despite Dani Olmo's excellent display in midweek.

Karim Adeyemi was the star of the show against Racing and has won the left wing starting job over Anthony Gordon at least for now, so we think he'll start once again alongside captain Raphinha and in-form Lamine Yamal in a high-flying front three.

articles.title: Tallon Griekspoor predicts how many Grand Slams Alexander Zverev could win after making scathing comments about him
articles.summary: Tallon Griekspoor has not held back when discussing Alexander Zverev’s US Open victory. Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the US Open final to win his...
articles.body:
Tallon Griekspoor has not held back when discussing Alexander Zverev's US Open victory.

Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the US Open final to win his second Grand Slam title after also lifting the Roland Garros title earlier this year.

Despite winning two Grand Slam titles this year, Zverev faced only one top 10 player , Shelton , in either tournament.

Partly as a result of this, Zverev's US Open victory has split opinion , and fellow ATP player Tallon Griekspoor has certainly not held back in what he thinks about it.

Tallon Griekspoor admits he has a hard time watching Alexander Zverev

Griekspoor, who beat Zverev at the Canadian Open , has not won a single Grand Slam match this entire year.

As the Dutchman prepares to represent his country in the Davis Cup , he had some strong words to say about the goings-on at the US Open this year ahead of his nation's tie against Colombia.

As reported by Ubitennis, Griekspoor gave his thoughts on the men's US Open final, in which he claimed Zverev 'wasn't exceptional'.

"I expected it against Shelton," Griekspoor said about Zverev's win. "The precedents were obviously already clearly in favour of Zverev. I found the match rather mediocre . Shelton played very inconsistently and gave away two or three free points per game. You see what a first Slam final can do to a player."

Griekspoor added, "Zverev wasn't exceptional , but he served really well. The second set tie-break was crucial."

One of the other big talking points surrounding Zverev was his ball bouncing before serving , something that prompted some of his opponents to complain.

Griekspoor was also not a fan of this, but he suggested that he has never particularly enjoyed watching Zverev.

"There were other sports going on, and I simply have a hard time watching Zverev," Griekspoor responded when asked if he watched Zverev.

"Especially in this tournament, where he bounced the ball 400 times before every serve. It was really extreme, but it obviously helped him. Maybe I should do the same."

Tallon Griekspoor does not think Alexander Zverev can challenge Jannik Sinner

Griekspoor was simply not done there, as he continued his strong remarks about Zverev and the US Open.

This included claiming that Carlos Alcaraz should have beaten Shelton in the quarter-finals, but Griekspoor believes the Spaniard was satisfied with how his first tournament in nearly five months went after returning from a wrist injury.

"Alcaraz should have beaten him in the quarter-finals, but he played a nightmare tiebreak in the fifth set," claimed Griekspoor.

"Then Alcaraz walked off the court smiling. I felt like that showed what his expectations were. He hadn't come into the tournament in top form. I think he and his team were already satisfied with that."

Zverev has won more Grand Slam titles than any other ATP player this year, and there is now discussion over whether he will be able to compete with both Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner next year when they are both fit.

The German is also in a good position to overtake Sinner as the world number one, but Griekspoor is very clear on whether he thinks this will happen. However, Griekspoor does believe that if openings in Grand Slam draws happen again, Zverev could win more major titles in the future.

"Absolutely not," responded Griekspoor. "There's not a hair on my head that thinks so. I hope they [Sinner and Alcaraz] both return to great levels very soon.

"But if those two were to fail during a tournament, Zverev is always the one who is ready. It wouldn't surprise me at all if he ended his career with four or five Slams."

articles.title: WTF?!? Jack Swagger Literally Cries Blood In Latest Power Slap Loss
articles.summary: Uhh … what the f—k was that?!? Former WWE champion Jack Swagger — real name Jake Hager — is no stranger to combat sports. After his WWE career, Hager joined...
articles.body:
Former WWE champion Jack Swagger — real name Jake Hager — is no stranger to combat sports. After his WWE career, Hager joined the Bellator MMA roster as a Heavyweight, relying on his collegiate wrestling background to build up a pro record of 3-0 (1). After his career in the cage stalled out , Hager raised eyebrows by signing a six-fight deal with Power Slap .

Hager's slap stint began with a successfully debut back in April, which ended with a big knockout win . Unfortunately, his sophomore appearance resulted in a nasty knockout loss just two months ago, and yet he's already back to competition.

This latest trip to the podium resulted in a second-round doctor stoppage loss that's one of the more bizarre things I've ever seen covering combat sports. After absorbing his opponent's slap and remaining conscious, Hager was clearly in a lot of pain. As he winced and limped a few stays away, red fluid began to leak from his tear ducts.

"He hit me right in the eye," Hager said dejectedly.

Just a few days ago, Demetrious Johnson explained why the risk of blindness wasn't worth Tom Aspinall trying to return to action to recapture his UFC Heavyweight title. Imagine undergoing that same risk for the handful of pennies slappers are paid, as well as the complete lack of respect and adoration from the general combat sports community.

articles.title: Schalke’s El-Faouzi chooses Morocco amid Germany interest
articles.summary: Schalke midfielder Soufiane El-Faouzi has been called up by Morocco for the upcoming international window, seemingly ending speculation over a possible futur...
articles.body:
Schalke midfielder Soufiane El-Faouzi has been called up by Morocco for the upcoming international window, seemingly ending speculation over a possible future with Germany .

The 24-year-old was recently considered a potential surprise candidate for new Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp's first squad. El-Faouzi, who was born in Siegen and holds both German and Moroccan citizenship, has instead been included in Morocco's 29-man squad.

The midfielder already made his Morocco debut in May , featuring in a 5-0 friendly win over Burundi. However, because it was only a friendly, he had remained eligible to switch to Germany. A competitive appearance against Gabon or Lesotho would end that possibility.

Morocco will face Gabon on September 25 and Lesotho four days later in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying. A friendly against Ghana will follow on October 4.

El-Faouzi has become an important player for Schalke since joining the club in summer 2025 and was reportedly among the dual nationals Klopp's Germany staff had been monitoring.

Meanwhile, Morocco coach Mohamed Ouahbi has also spoken about Younes Ebnoutalib , who accepted an invitation from Klopp and is expected to represent Germany. Ouahbi said Morocco had monitored the Eintracht Frankfurt striker since last season and that he had personally explained the country's project to the player.

The coach added that Ebnoutalib had made his decision and that Morocco would now move forward.

articles.summary: With "GameDay" in Oxford, ESPN seems to have found the perfect celebrity guest picker.
articles.body:
With the "College GameDay" crew in Oxford for Week 3, ESPN seems to have found the perfect celebrity guest picker.

On Thursday, Pat McAfee announced on his show that 89-year-old star actor Morgan Freeman will be joining "GameDay" on Saturday ahead of Ole Miss vs. LSU, one of the most highly-anticipated games of the season.

Initially, Freeman may appear to be a rather random selection by ESPN — but with his Ole Miss ties, it's clear who he'll be rooting for in Saturday's game.

Here's what to know about Freeman's Ole Miss fandom.

It doesn't take much detective work to understand why Freeman has established himself as a Rebels fan. While he was born in Memphis, Tennessee, a young Freeman was raised in Mississippi; as an infant, he was sent to live with his paternal grandmother in Charleston. Throughout Freeman's youth, he also lived in Greenwood, Mississippi, before moved to Indiana and Chicago.

In the many years since he became a celebrity, Freeman has remained involved in Mississippi politics, charitable endeavors and more. In 2021, he played a role in $1 million being donated to Ole Miss, establishing the Center for Evidence-Based Policing and Reform. Freeman also reportedly still lives in Charleston, Mississippi.

When it comes to Rebels athletics, Freeman has frequently been spotted in attendance at Ole Miss basketball games.

Now, he'll sit alongside McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit and the "GameDay" crew, ready to support his Rebels in one of the games of the year.

Why It Matters: Considered a borderline bust after two middling seasons, Coleman emerged from obscurity on Thursday night to catch six passes for 63 yards and help pick up the slack offensively after DJ Moore (shoulder) was lost to a shoulder injury. If Moore is OK, there's no need to make a move for now, though Thursday's proof of life should at least put Coleman back on your radar.

articles.title: Commanders put Mike Sainristil on the hot seat
articles.summary: Dan Quinn and Daronte Jones have expressed confidence in Mike Sainristil, but Washington's latest move sends another message.
articles.body:
Are the Washington Commanders sending a message to third-year cornerback Mike Sainristil ? Earlier this week, head coach Dan Quinn essentially called out Sainristil in his press conference regarding his play in Sunday's season-opening loss to the Philadelphia Eagles .

"The touchdown play definitely felt like, as the motion got over, man, like, you have to go get set," Quinn said on Monday. "And those are things that we have to get corrected. We've definitely identified a few things that, 'Hey, man, these are the things that we have to get corrected.' Mike's a very good competitor. I'm certain that we will, but to have that type of play and just not have the right focus at the right time, completely not acceptable."

Quinn was right, but this is something he never does. Quinn always protects his players. Sainristil allowed two big plays in Sunday's game, and in one of them he looked completely lost or disinterested. That play upset Quinn.

Washington's second-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Sainristil enjoyed a solid rookie season. He regressed last season, and questions remained about whether he fit best outside or in the slot.

For his part, Sainristil didn't shy away from his Week 1 performance and took accountability.

"Honestly, I'm not somebody that sits there, whether I played good or bad," Sainristil said this week. "I'm not somebody who is going to sit there and sulk in it. So, for the people who think that is what I am doing, that's the complete opposite. I am not that type of person. I can assure you [of] that. But for me, it is just focusing on 'What can I do to be better?' every single day. Whether I play good or bad."

Quinn expressed confidence in Sainristil on Wednesday.

"I've got a lot of confidence in Mike. I really do," Quinn said. "I love him. And I'm certain that he'll be one leveling up on plays that he knows can be controlled. Somebody beats you on a good play, man, we tip our hat. But that's the spot that we wanna see, just, man, staying in constant things that he can control: the call, the technique, and that. I've got a lot of confidence in him. I'm certain that'll get done."

Sainristil better be ready this week. The Commanders face the Cowboys and their receivers, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . There may be no better wide receiver duo in all of the NFL. And with Washington already without Trey Amos until at least Week 5, GM Adam Peters made a move on Thursday, signing veteran cornerback Isaac Yiadom from the practice squad.

Did the Commanders make this move because they're worried about Sainristil, or is it to add depth against a team that will throw the ball a lot?

Here's what defensive coordinator Daronte Jones said about Sainristil:

"He wasn't satisfied with the way he played, and I don't think anyone was, but yet and still, we know what he's capable of," Jones said.

After signing Yiadom from the practice squad, the Commanders now have five cornerbacks on the roster: Sainristil, Yiadom, Amik Robertson , Fabian Moreau and Rasul Douglas .

If Sainristil struggles again on Sunday, Washington can't afford to let him play through it. Now, the Commanders have options.

articles.title: Watertown soccer teams sweep SF Roosevelt with regular-season winding down
articles.summary: Watertown's soccer teams improved to 10-0-1 (boys) and 6-4-1 (girls) with home soccer wins over Sioux Falls Roosevelt on Sept. 17, 2026.
articles.body:
Watertown soccer teams sweep SF Roosevelt with regular-season winding down

WATERTOWN — Watertown High School's boys and girls soccer teams continued what could be historic seasons with victories over Sioux Falls Roosevelt on Thursday, Sept. 18, 2026, at the Allen Mitchell Athletic Complex.

The Arrow girls (6-4-1) opened the evening with a 2-0 win and the boys (10-0-1) closed it by rallying for a 4-1 victory. In between games, 22 seniors (16 boys and six girls) were honored along with their parents on Senior Night.

Roosevelt didn't make things easy for Watertown's boys. Aaron Schroeder scored with 14:56 left in the first half to give the Rough Riders a 1-0 lead. Watertown pulled even on Xane Fligge's goal with 17 seconds remaining in the half.

Carson Schlaht added two goals and Ethan Raml one in the second half for the fourth-rated Arrows. Schlaht and Matthew Bertsch each added assists and goalie Owen Muller notched four saves.

"After Roosevelt scored the first goal, our boys didn't hang their heads or point fingers, they actually came together in huddle on our own end. When they broke that huddle, the switch was turned on," Watertown boys' coach Jesse Hauck said. "The last 10 minutes of the of the first half and the entire second half was who we are."

Sophia Gallardo scored with just over four minutes remaining in the first half and added another goal less than three minutes into the second half to propel Watertown's girls.

Big goals within reach for Watertown's boys

The Arrow boys went 6-4-5 a year ago and entered the state Class AA playoffs as the No. 12 seed. They upset Sioux Falls Washington 2-1 in the first round before falling to No. 13 Brandon Valley 4-3 in the quarterfinals.

With such a large returning cast and so much experience, the Arrows have been near-perfect all season with the exception of a 0-0 draw at Harrisburg on Aug. 29.

Watertown, at 5-0-1, has its sights set on winning its first Eastern South Dakota Conference championship since the Arrows started playing SDHSAA-sanctioned Class AA soccer in 2014. They'll need to win out, with home games 9-22 against Brookings and 9-24 against Mitchell, and also beat No. 5 Aberdeen Central on the road on 9-29 to accomplish the feat. Aberdeen Central is 6-1 in the ESD, including a 3-0 win over Harrisburg.

"We have three solid ESD games left to finish the regular season with more goals to complete after that," Hauck said.

The Arrows have many weapons on offense led by Roger Carranza (12 goals, five assists), Isaac Thorson (nine goals, two assists), Fligge (seven goals, seven assists), Luke McLaughlin (four goals) and Schlaht (two goals, four assists). The defense has also been stellar with Muller (45 saves on the season) representing the final barrier for opponents.

"This season has been about depth and unite. It's also about no matter the situation, we feel like we can overcome any obstacle in our way," Hauck said. "This group has been together since they were little and has added some key pieces along the way. It's not always pretty, but when this group flips the switch it's amazing to watch."

Watertown is currently the No. 2 seed in the state Class AA standings and is in position to host at least one, if not more, playoff games scheduled for Oct. 6, 10 and 13.

The Arrows have been played for a state title, but would certainly love the opportunity this fall since the state Class A and AA soccer champions are scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 17 at the Allen Mitchell Athletic Complex.

Watertown's girls also producing a quality season

At 6-4-1 overall and 3-3 in the ESD, the Arrow girls haven't matched the boys but are having a very notable season in their own right. Watertown went 8-7-1 last fall and upset sixth-seeded Sioux Falls Lincoln for its first playoff win since becoming a sanctioned program in 2014.

After the win over Roosevelt, the Arrows currently stand seventh in the state Class AA standings and are in position to host a playoff game for the first time.

Like the boys, the seniors have provided good leadership but the team is also receiving key contributions from a number of underclassmen.

One of those is Gallardo, a freshman forward-midfielder, who leads the team with 16 goals. She also has five assists. Other leaders include senior Katie Fischer (nine goals, six assists), junior Bo Meidinger (six goals, one assist) and senior Claire Schochenmaier (three goals, four assists). Enstad, another senior, handles net-guarding duties (more than 70 saves) for a defense that features seniors Arianna Snyder, Olivia Dettman and Harper Hendricks.

The Arrow girls have the same remaining regular-season schedule as the Arrow boys. It's interesting to note that the team's four losses have come to the top four teams in the Class AA standings: No. 1 Harrisburg, No. 2 Pierre, No. 3 Rapid City Stevens and No. 4 Yankton. They also drew with No. 6 O'Gorman. The regular-season finale will be against No. 5 Aberdeen Central.

At first, it wasn't clear what exactly had happened to DJ Moore .

After Josh Allen tried to find him with a pass in the end zone on Thursday night for the Buffalo Bills , the long-time Carolina Panthers wide receiver stayed down.

Only on the replay was it clear that Moore had gotten himself injured.

And only when the crowd at the brand new Highmark Stadium went particularly quiet was it clear that Moore wasn't getting up right away, either.

Moore appeared to hit his upper body hard on the ground as he came down through contact on his catch attempt.

It was his left shoulder area that smashed into the ground particularly hard, and that potentially was turned in an awkward position, too.

Once on the ground, Moore clearly was holding at his shoulder area, as can be seen in the picture at the top of this article.

The worst fear for such a motion from Moore would be a broken collarbone, but it's not clear yet what may have happened.

The Bills ruled Moore out relatively quickly, terming it a shoulder injury.

Buffalo went on to win the game, but it could end up feeling like a somewhat empty victory if Moore is forced to miss extended time.

Three years after the Panthers traded Moore to the Chicago Bears , it was the Bears who traded Moore to Buffalo this offseason.

He's getting a chance to reprise the WR1 role he had with Carolina. Allen hadn't had a true No. 1 WR in the last couple seasons, essentially since Stefon Diggs left the Bills.

Moore and Allen had showed good early chemistry, but this could ruin all of that if the news is bad.

Moore has dealt with a variety of injuries since entering the NFL with the Panthers.

His first ailment that forced him to miss a game was a concussion in 2019.

In 2020, he had a Grade 2 ankle sprain that kept him out of a game.

In 2021, Moore dealt with a tailbone bruise and a hamstring sprain, neither of which resulted in a missed game.

Moore strained his knee in 2022 and again didn't miss a game.

He had a small ankle sprain in 2023, then a quad strain in 2024 and a groin pull in 2025. All of those injuries didn't force Moore to miss subsequent action.

In essence, Moore hasn't missed a full game due to injury since the 2020 season with Carolina.

His reliability was a key part of his acquisition by the Bills, but this is still football, and there's no telling what can happen on any given play.

Buffalo's fans will be hoping for the best, and former fans of Moore in Carolina and Chicago will be waiting to see what the full scoop is.

articles.title: Five players who could freshen up Thomas Tuchel’s England squad
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel will name his first England squad since the 2026 World Cup this morning ahead of the upcoming internationals.England begin their UEFA Nations L...
articles.body:
Thomas Tuchel will name his first England squad since the 2026 World Cup this morning ahead of the upcoming internationals.

England begin their UEFA Nations League campaign with clashes against Spain , Czechia and Croatia , as the Three Lions start a new cycle.

As England look to bounce back from the disappointment of a semi-final loss in the summer, we've picked five players who could freshen up the squad this month.

Cole Palmer was a headline omission in the summer with the Chelsea midfielder snubbed after a mixed campaign at club level.

Palmer's recent admission that he was on 'one leg for 10 months' showed the extent to which his body had failed him, but a full summer off and pre-season looks to have brought back his spark.

Palmer has been excellent in the opening weeks of the season, forming an exciting understanding with summer arrival Morgan Rogers at Chelsea. Is that a partnership that Tuchel could look to replicate with England?

Morgan Gibbs-White can count himself unfortunate to have missed the World Cup, with the Nottingham Forest midfielder not selected despite a brilliant run of form during the run-in.

Gibbs-White scored nine times in the final 10 Premier League games and ended the campaign with 15 league goals, a league-leading total among English midfielders. He's started the new season in good form and, despite strong competition in his position, deserves a chance.

Thomas Tuchel used five different options at right-back during England's World Cup campaign, as the position became a problem. Reece James sustained an injury, while Ezri Konsa and Jarell Quansah were both used as makeshift options in his absence.

All the while, Trent Alexander-Arnold watched on from his holidays. Alexander-Arnold is a unique talent, but the Real Madrid right-back has struggled to convince multiple England managers. Could the start of a new cycle offer him another route back in?

Rio Ngumoha made his England debut ahead of the 2026 World Cup after being invited to train with the group pre-tournament.

The teenager became the fifth-youngest England debutant ever, recognition for a breakout season at Liverpool . Electric with the ball at his feet, Ngumoha looks likely to be a long-term fixture in England squads. Is this month an ideal time to continue his integration?

Were it not for Jarrad Branthwaite's pesky hamstrings, there's an argument he'd be a regular with England. As it is, the 24-year-old has just a single cap, despite being one of the most talented central defenders in the country.

Back fit and thriving at Everton , he'll hope he's done enough during an unbeaten start to the Premier League season to get the nod.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola favourite to make Liverpool audition this weekend
articles.summary: Liverpool enjoyed another busy transfer window this summer, adding several top talents to Andoni Iraola's squad.The arrivals of Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz...
articles.body:
Liverpool enjoyed another busy transfer window this summer, adding several top talents to Andoni Iraola 's squad.

The arrivals of Jeremy Jacquet , Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola were instant boosts to the quality of the squad, but a number of departures led to many supporters feeling that the side remains a work in progress.

Mohamed Salah , Andrew Robertson , Ibrahima Konate and Curtis Jones were the four biggest exits in the window and the Reds' midfield has been left suffering as a result.

With the winter window now a topic of discussion in recruitment meetings across the country, Liverpool's next midfielder could be set to make his audition this weekend.

Liverpool's fourth £100 million signing is an Iraola favourite

Neither Liverpool's attack nor backline have been perfect this campaign, but they both seem to be in a much better place than the midfield.

The Reds have lacked balance in the middle of the park, and a fresh face in the midfield looks necessary if Liverpool are serious about competing on multiple fronts again.

Luckily for Iraola and the recruitment team at Anfield, Liverpool will get to take a good look this weekend at the player many believe will be the club's next midfielder, Alex Scott .

Scott plays for Iraola's former side Bournemouth and has become one of the most talked about players in the Premier League over the last 18 months.

According to transfer insider David Ornstein , it will likely take a fee of over £100 million to prise the Englishman away from The Cherries, and Liverpool will get the perfect opportunity to assess if the 23-year-old is worth that price tag at the Vitality Stadium on Sunday.

Scott's quality is clear to see but a great performance against the Reds could be what it takes to seal his move to Merseyside.

Liverpool will not be unopposed however, with Manchester United and Chelsea both reportedly keeping tabs on the midfielder, but Iraola's relationship with Scott could become key in the race for his signature.

With Liverpool chasing only their second win of the Premier League campaign, Alex Scott has the opportunity to show Liverpool exactly why he needs to become their fourth £100m signing on Sunday.

articles.title: Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez launches homer No. 40 in an MVP-caliber season. 'Numbers don't lie'
articles.summary: Yordan Alvarez becomes just the fifth Houston Astro to hit 40 homers in a season and keeps MVP and Triple Crown hopes alive.
articles.body:
Number 40 elicited no fanfare from the man who hit it. After his fifth-inning blast landed in Daikin Park's second deck, Yordan Alvarez rounded the bases with an impassive expression. The hint of a smile crossed it as he reached home plate and bashed forearms with Isaac Paredes . Yet no movement suggested a milestone to Jeremy Peña , who awaited the slugger with a hug at the end of the Houston Astros dugout.

Just four other men in Houston franchise history have mounted a 40-home run season. Jeff Bagwell did it three times, Lance Berkman twice and Richard Hidalgo and Alex Bregman each once. Alvarez joined their company Thursday, his benchmark swing aiding an Astros home-run barrage in a 6-2 win over the Royals and providing his prolific season with the kind of flourish his understated personality would not.

"It's special," said Peña, the Astros shortstop and leadoff hitter. "Because last year he dealt with a lot of injuries and a lot of people - I'm not going to say they forgot about him, but they kind of did. They kind of forgot about Yordan.

"I know that he took it personal. He took it upon himself to take care of his body this year and stay on the field, stay healthy. And he knows that when he's healthy, he can put up MVP numbers. He's shown it this year and it's special to watch."

Alvarez hit his 35th home run on July 28. That he required 42 more games to record his 40th, a stretch in which the Astros' offense ebbed along with their 1-2 lineup punch, perhaps opened up the race for the award Peña mentioned. Rays third baseman Junior Caminero and Yankees ace Cam Schlittler have both garnered public support in the AL Most Valuable Player discussion in recent days.

Both of their clubs own records superior to that of Houston, which is 77-76 and clinging to a one-game lead in the AL West . That Alvarez is a primary reason the Astros are even in a playoff hunt is something even their manager does not dispute. Few teams could withstand removal of a Triple Crown candidate, much less one on which every other hitter had an OPS under .800 before Thursday's game.

"Our club, without him, would be a completely different record," manager Joe Espada said. "Obviously, credit to our players. This is a team, everybody contributes. But without Yordan, we could be in a completely different spot."

Alvarez entered Thursday with a win probability added value 3.0 points higher than the next-closest AL hitter, Ben Rice of the Yankees, per Baseball Reference. Since 1910, just seven AL or NL hitters have led their league in win probability added by that wide a margin over a full season: Barry Bonds, Babe Ruth, Ted Williams, Mickey Mantle, Willie McCovey, Al Simmons and Ty Cobb.

Among AL hitters, Alvarez entered Thursday with a 116-point lead in OPS, a 33-point lead in adjusted OPS-plus and a 34-point lead in runs created, per Baseball Reference. The list of players who have led their league by as wide a margin in all three of those categories for a full season: Aaron Judge , Bonds, Williams, Ruth, Stan Musial, Rogers Hornsby, Mark McGwire and Nap Lajoie.

"Forty homers is impressive," said Astros outfielder Taylor Trammell . "But to do it while hitting .300-plus, that means he's a complete hitter in my book, and he's unreal.

"I'm not discrediting anybody, I think there's a lot of guys in that MVP race that are really good. But when he comes up to the plate, every single time it's like we have a good chance to win or get back in the game or whatever it is. And every time he's just clutch. It can be a hit, it can be a homer, it can be a walk, whatever it is. He's a complete hitter."

Bias is natural in the Astros' clubhouse, but their offense's trajectory is instructive. From Aug. 3 through Sunday, the Astros scored the third-fewest runs in the majors. Alvarez batted .242 with three homers in 35 games in that stretch. Peña, the lineup's sparkplug, posted a .170 average and a .518 OPS over his 35 games in the same span.

Both stirred in a three-game series against Kansas City that reflected their indispensability to any hopes the Astros have of a playoff run. Peña went 8-for-13 in the series with three home runs. Alvarez went 4-for-10 with two home runs. The duo combined for all four of Houston's hits in a series-opening win and two of the five solo home runs it recorded in the finale Thursday.

Peña homered on the first pitch a Royals starter threw in two of the three games. In addition to picking good locations, Espada said he thought Peña was "in a good posture to hit those pitches." Peña said he found a better position from which to deliver his swing and "do damage on my pitches," partly through early on-field hitting sessions with Alvarez the first two days.

Thursday, Peña hit his 20th home run this season on a first-pitch sinker from Seth Lugo . Daulton Varsho and LaMonte Wade Jr. also homered before Alvarez struck his 40th on a Lugo fastball in the fifth inning. Trammell added a solo shot in the eighth for the Astros, who ended the night with a one-game division lead over the Rangers, over whom they own the tiebreaker.

"Obviously, Yordan's our horse," Peña said. "Where he goes, we go. And he's been doing it all year. He's been carrying us all year."

It is an opportunity Alvarez was denied last season. A hand fracture and ankle sprain limited him to 48 games for an Astros team that fell one win short of the playoffs. This year has illustrated the difference that most likely made.

Alvarez ended Thursday with a 1.027 OPS, over 70 points ahead of any other qualified major-hitter. A shot at the second Triple Crown in the majors since 1967 remained in play. Alvarez was tied for first in the AL in average (.311) with the Rays' Chandler Simpson . His 99 RBIs trailed AL leader Pete Alonso by three. His 40th home run put him one behind Caminero, with nine games left in Houston's season.

"I'm a believer in: numbers don't lie," Peña said. "Numbers don't lie. And yes, they're going to say he's a DH. But at the end of the day, what he's doing, it's above and beyond."

articles.title: Elding ready for Irish chance after passport delay
articles.summary: Hibernian striker Owen Elding will hope to make his mark after receiving his first official call-up to the Republic of Ireland senior squad for the start of...
articles.body:
Hibernian striker Owen Elding's first official call-up to the Republic of Ireland senior squad for the start of their Nations League campaign was a long time coming.

The 20-year-old was included in Heimir Hallgrimsson's squad for friendlies against Qatar and Canada in May and June, but only as a training player.

He was ineligible to feature in those games as he was still waiting for his Irish citizenship to come through, but Hallgrimsson invited him into camp to get a better look at the youngster.

Elding was born in England but has lived in the Republic of Ireland from the age of six, when his family made the move after his father, Anthony, signed for Sligo Rovers.

He therefore qualified for the Republic of Ireland on residency grounds and he began the process of applying for Irish citizenship last year, but there was a bizarre reason for the delay that left him unable to pull on the green shirt in the last international window.

The fuel protests in the Republic of Ireland in April led to the cancellation of a mandatory ceremony to receive his Irish passport.

With said passport now in hand, Elding is hoping to make his long-awaited Republic of Ireland debut in this extended four-game window.

Owen, like his father Anthony, played for Sligo Rovers after coming through the club's academy.

He made his debut as a 17-year-old in October 2023 and then enjoyed a breakout season in the Irish Premier Division in 2025, scoring 16 goals and providing five assists on his way to winning the PFAI Young Player of the Year award that season.

His form for Sligo attracted interest from across the Irish Sea and Scottish Premiership side Hibs swooped in to sign him in January of this year on a four-and-a-half year deal.

The striker has impressed since moving to Scotland , scoring six goals in 22 games, including three in nine outings in the current campaign.

His call-up to the summer window allowed him time to integrate with the squad and also whetted his appetite for more involvement going forward.

"Definitely getting that experience with the first-team international set-up was massive," he said in August.

"Obviously I couldn't play the game but it was just a chance for me to go in and show the staff and everyone what I could do.

"Just being around the boys for the camp and seeing what it's like is something I want to be a part of."

He certainly left an impression on Hallgrimsson, who has included him in the squad for games against Kosovo and Austria either side of a double-header against Israel in a 12-day stretch.

While his involvement may be limited this window as he works his way back to full fitness after a recent injury and competes with in-form and established forwards Troy Parrott , Adam Idah and Tom Cannon, Hallgrimsson is certainly excited about Elding's potential.

"He really impressed us with his attitude and his character and how he presented himself as a player," said the Icelander.

"He has been struggling with injury, he's been coming back, but you can see the quality this kid has."

articles.title: Pressure on Wolves - will Albion rock Molineux?
articles.summary: Fan writer Jonny Drury wonders whether a young West Bromwich Albion side can upset fierce rivals Wolverhampton Wanderers.
articles.body:
The first Black Country derby in the league for some time - and the first in front of fans for 14 years. No wonder there is so much anticipation around this one.

You have to go back to 2008 to find the last time the two sides met in the second tier and the situation was very different back then.

Albion were the ones who went on to win the title but this time the tables are very much turned.

Wolves are the big fish down from the top flight and Albion are the young pups looking to impress.

They have done that this season and sit above Wolves, after an impressive start.

But make no mistake, the pressure is on Wolves, the onus is on Wolves to take the game to Albion at Molineux and win.

They have not had the most convincing start and a victory over the old rivals would certainly kickstart their campaign.

But that pressure being on Wolves may just play into Albion's favour. They can play with freedom, soak up pressure and hit on the break, something they are good at.

And the atmosphere will be key on the day. Molineux can rock when it is going well, but if Albion edge ahead early on, it could turn and play in their favour.

A fascinating afternoon is in store on Sunday.

articles.title: European Le Mans Series: The Affordable Race Weekend That Is Totally Worth It
articles.summary: "It gave me an F1-weekend feeling, but with a lot more access."
articles.body:
If you love Formula 1 but have always wanted to get closer to the cars, drivers, and teams without spending a small fortune, there is another race weekend you might want to add to your list.I spent the weekend covering the European Le Mans Series at Silverstone as accredited media and, at times, it had all the ingredients of an F1 weekend: busy grandstands, professional teams, drivers from around the world and millions of pounds' worth of racing machinery competing at one of Britain's most famous circuits.Except there was one major difference: the level of access available to ordinary fans.And I mean really close.

You could do an entire weekend for as little as £35

For the 2026 Silverstone event, a three-day weekend ticket started at just £35 during the Super Early Bird period.Friday tickets started at £10, while Saturday and Sunday could each be had for £20. Even if you decided to turn up and buy a three-day ticket at the circuit, the published on-the-day price was £50.Selected grandstand access was included on a first-come, first-served basis, and children under 16 could attend free when accompanied by an adult.But here's where things became particularly interesting.For another £10, fans could add the Platinum option, which included access to the Sunday pit walk, autograph session and pre-race grid walk.So someone who secured the £35 early weekend ticket and added Platinum could potentially have spent £45 for three days at Silverstone with experiences that can feel decidedly VIP at other major sporting events.

The accessibility wasn't limited to organised sessions.Walking through the paddock, I watched fans approach team personnel, ask questions about the cars and wish them luck ahead of the race.At times, it felt more like a petrol station car meet than an international motorsport event.Except you would look around and remember that these weren't modified road cars gathering on a Sunday afternoon.These were professional racing teams preparing millions of pounds' worth of machinery to compete at Silverstone.You could also find yourself walking past a driver and simply start a conversation.Drivers stopped to speak with supporters, posed for selfies and signed autographs. What impressed me was how receptive and patient many of them appeared to be with the people who had come to watch them race.

You could literally walk onto the starting grid

Then came what was probably one of the most impressive experiences available to fans: the grid walk.Before the race, supporters with the Platinum upgrade were allowed onto the Silverstone grid, where cars from LMP2, LMP2 Pro/Am, LMP3, and LMGT3 were assembled ahead of the start.Imagine walking through a multimillion-pound car show where almost nothing is behind a rope.Fans could stand alongside the cars, pose for photographs, peer into cockpits and get close enough to appreciate details that are almost impossible to see from a grandstand or through a television screen.And shortly afterwards, those same cars were racing around Silverstone.

F1 fans might recognise a few people too

If you're coming to ELMS from Formula 1, there are likely to be some familiar names on the entry list.At Silverstone, that included Jamie Chadwick, the three-time W Series champion and former Williams Racing Driver Academy member, who competed in the top LMP2 category for IDEC Sport.She wasn't the only driver with links to the F1 world.Pietro Fittipaldi, who made two Formula 1 starts for Haas, was also competing in LMP2, while the field featured several drivers who have raced in categories such as Formula 2 and Formula 3.It means you aren't necessarily watching a field of completely unfamiliar drivers. Some have already been part of the Formula 1 world, while others have travelled through the same junior categories that produced many of the drivers currently on the F1 grid.The difference is that here, you might subsequently bump into one of them while walking through the paddock.

There is almost always something happening on the track

This might have been my favourite part.ELMS isn't one class of car circulating around the track. Four classes race simultaneously, each effectively fighting its own race while sharing the same piece of tarmac.That means you could have an LMP2 battle unfolding while the leaders negotiate their way through slower traffic, with separate fights taking place in LMP2 Pro/Am, LMP3 and LMGT3 at exactly the same time.There are races within the race.For a spectator, it means there is almost always something to watch.You might be following a fight for the overall lead one moment and, seconds later, see a prototype trying to find its way around a GT car while another battle develops behind them.The traffic isn't an inconvenience. Managing it is part of endurance racing, and watching cars with dramatically different levels of performance negotiate the same circuit adds another layer to the spectacle.

Some of these teams are racing for a route to Le Mans

There is also considerably more at stake than simply winning another motor race.The European Le Mans Series forms part of the pathway to the 24 Hours of Le Mans, one of the most famous endurance races in the world.At the end of the 2026 season, the LMP2 champion and runner-up will earn automatic invitations to compete in LMP2 at the 2027 24 Hours of Le Mans. The LMP2 Pro/Am champion also receives an LMP2 invitation, while the LMP3 champion earns an invitation to step up to LMP2 and the LMGT3 champion receives an invitation in its category.That puts the fan access into perspective.The team member answering your question in the paddock or the driver posing for a selfie could be competing for an opportunity to race at Le Mans.

It gave me an F1-weekend feeling, but with a lot more access

I've attended Formula 1 weekends, and I'm not suggesting ELMS is trying to replace F1. They are very different championships and very different forms of motorsport.But there were moments at Silverstone when the overall experience felt surprisingly familiar.You have professional teams, serious racing machinery, drivers from around the world, recognisable names, busy grandstands and the atmosphere of a major motorsport weekend.Then ELMS adds something increasingly difficult to find at the highest levels of sport: proximity.You can walk through the paddock. You can speak to team members. You can meet drivers. With the right ticket, you can walk through the pit lane and stand on the starting grid alongside the cars you're about to watch race.And because four classes are competing together, there can be an extraordinary amount of action happening on the circuit at any given moment.For an F1 fan wanting to experience another side of motorsport without spending hundreds of pounds just to get through the gate, that's a compelling proposition.It manages to feel like an elite motorsport experience without making the average fan feel like they have to be a VIP to properly experience it.I went to Silverstone to cover the European Le Mans Series.I left wondering why more motorsport fans aren't talking about it.If you're putting together your motorsport bucket list, ELMS deserves a spot on it.
